claims.claim: At an interval of four months from Gregory's return, in the year 637 of the era of Theopolis, about the third hour of the night, an earthquake shook the city 'at the time when I was celebrating my marriage with a young maiden, and the whole city was making rejoicings and holding a festival at the public cost'; it levelled 'by far the greater part of the buildings' and 'all the portions of the most holy church were thrown to the ground, with the exception of the hemisphere'
claims.witness: Evagrius, Ecclesiastical History VI.8, tr. Walford (evagrius-scholasticus walford1846 l.11452-11463; OCR 'Av an interval'); Greek Bidez-Parmentier l.20931-20940

claims.claim: Walford's page heading dates the earthquake and wedding 'A.D. 589'; Evagrius gives only the era year 637
claims.witness: Walford's running head (evagrius-scholasticus walford1846 l.11467)

claims.claim: 'Evagrius was a native of Epiphania on the Orontes, and his birth may be fixed about a.p. [A.D.] 536. He was by profession a Scholasticus, or advocate, and by this title he is commonly distinguished from other persons of the same name'
claims.witness: Walford, Account of the Author (evagrius-scholasticus walford1846 l.327-331; OCR 'a.p.')

claims.claim: Photius: 'Evagrius Scholasticus, an ex-praefect, born at Epiphania in Coele-Syria, in six books', beginning where Socrates and Theodoret end and going 'down to the twelfth year of the reign of the emperor Maurice'
claims.witness: Photius, Library cod. 29, tr. Freese (photius_library-v1_freese1920 l.2410-2413; OCR 'Histoi-y')

claims.claim: He is a different man from the monk Evagrius Ponticus, whose Praktikos is held separately
claims.witness: evagrius_praktikos_dysinger.txt l.1 ('EVAGRIUS PONTICUS (EVAGRIOS PONTIKOS), THE PRAKTIKOS'); Walford l.329-331 on the title distinguishing him from namesakes

claims.claim: When the Apameans heard Antioch had been burnt, Bishop Thomas displayed the wood of the cross; 'my parents visited it together with the rest, accompanied by myself, at that time a school-boy'; as Thomas made the circuit of the sanctuary 'there followed him a large body of fire, blazing but not consuming'
claims.witness: Evagrius IV.26, tr. Walford (evagrius-scholasticus walford1846 l.8786-8819); Greek B-P l.16156-16170

claims.claim: The Persian king Chosroes took and burned Antioch before the Apamea display
claims.witness: Evagrius IV.25-26, tr. Walford (evagrius-scholasticus walford1846 l.8722-8760, 8790-8791)

claims.claim: Walford's page heading puts the Persian invasion and the capture of Antioch in 540
claims.witness: Walford running head (evagrius-scholasticus walford1846 l.8710)

claims.claim: 'Two years after the capture of Antioch by the Persians, a pestilence broke out'; 'at the commencement of this calamity I was seized with what are termed buboes, while still a school-boy, and lost by its recurrence at different times several of my children, my wife, and many of my kin'; 'not quite two years before my writing this, being now in the fifty-eighth year of my age ... I lost a daughter and her son'
claims.witness: Evagrius IV.29, tr. Walford (evagrius-scholasticus walford1846 l.8999-9001, 9034-9047); Greek B-P l.16562-16580 (γαμετὴν, no 'first')

claims.claim: Walford calls the wife lost to plague his 'first wife'
claims.witness: Walford, Account of the Author (evagrius-scholasticus walford1846 l.355); an inference from the later marriage, not Evagrius's word

claims.claim: 'On occasion also of my ponderings on the loss of my children, when I was perplexed with the suggestion, why such things did not befall heathens who had numerous offspring; although I had not disclosed my thoughts to any one, he wrote advising me to abandon such ideas as being displeasing to God' (Simeon the Stylite the Younger)
claims.witness: Evagrius VI.23, tr. Walford (evagrius-scholasticus walford1846 l.12108-12154); Greek B-P l.22020-22026

claims.claim: A banker charged Gregory, bishop of Theopolis, 'that he had had criminal intercourse with his own sister, married to another man'; Gregory went to the imperial city 'accompanied by myself as his adviser, and is victorious after a prolonged struggle' before the patriarchs, senate and metropolitans; the accuser was scourged, paraded and exiled
claims.witness: Evagrius VI.7, tr. Walford (evagrius-scholasticus walford1846 l.11386-11437); Greek B-P l.20872-20876; Evagrius calls himself Gregory's adviser, not his friend

claims.claim: Walford calls the charge 'a charge of incest'
claims.witness: Walford, Account of the Author (evagrius-scholasticus walford1846 l.361)

claims.claim: His memorials, mostly in Gregory's name, won him 'questorian rank' from Tiberius Constantine and 'that of prefecture' from Maurice Tiberius, for what he wrote when Maurice became father of Theodosius
claims.witness: Evagrius VI.24, tr. Walford (evagrius-scholasticus walford1846 l.12220-12229)

claims.claim: He compiled another volume of 'memorials, epistles, decrees, orations, and disputations'; Walford says the collection may be regarded as lost
claims.witness: Evagrius VI.24 (evagrius-scholasticus walford1846 l.12220-12222); Walford l.413-414

claims.claim: He writes for the side that held to Chalcedon: Nestorius is 'that God-assaulting tongue', whose 'impious blasphemy' prefaces the history; 'the impious Eutyches'
claims.witness: Evagrius I proem and I.9, tr. Walford (walford1846 l.1222-1236, 1721)

claims.claim: Photius: 'The style is not without charm, although somewhat diffuse; in matters of doctrine he is certainly more trustworthy than other historians. The work also contains some passages about images.'
claims.witness: Photius, Library cod. 29, tr. Freese (l.2413-2416); Photius as patriarch of Constantinople 858-867 and 878-886 in Freese's list (l.1025, 1284-1300)

claims.claim: 'Here let me close my history, in the twelfth year of the reign of Maurice Tiberius ... If any matter has been overlooked by me or has been treated without sufficient accuracy, let no one blame me'
claims.witness: Evagrius VI.24, tr. Walford (evagrius-scholasticus walford1846 l.12203-12209)

claims.claim: Walford: 'his style is frequently affected and redundant'; the credulity of his wonder stories 'ought therefore in no way to affect his reputation for honesty'; the work 'was used by Nicephorus Callisti' and noticed favourably by Photius
claims.witness: Walford, Account of the Author (evagrius-scholasticus walford1846 l.389-406)

claims.claim: Arndt and Krusch match stories of Gregory of Tours to Evagrius: 'de puero Iudaeo ... (= Evagrii Hist. eccl. IV, 2Q)' and 'Eadem Evagrius Schol., Hist. eccl. IV, 26 ... narravit'
claims.witness: gregory-tours_opera-mgh-srm-1-lat_arndt-krusch1885 l.35914, 38442 (OCR '2Q', 'Sclwl.')

claims.claim: Gregory's years: Walford's headings give 571 for his election and 594 for his death; Gallandi gives 'anno 570 ... usque ad annum 593'
claims.witness: Walford running heads (evagrius-scholasticus walford1846 l.10153, 12173); Gallandi's notice in Migne PG 88 (dorotheus-gaza ... migne-pg88 l.142063)

claims.claim: Walford's headings put the Apamea display in 540
claims.witness: Walford running head (evagrius-scholasticus walford1846 l.8774)

contested_claims.claim: The years of Gregory of Antioch's patriarchate
contested_claims.sides: Walford's running heads: elected 571, died 594 (walford1846 l.10153, 12173). Andrea Gallandi, notice reprinted in Migne PG 88: 570 to 593 (l.142063). Evagrius gives no year; he says Gregory died shortly before the twelfth year of Maurice, where he closes (l.12182-12204).

absent_details.note: No held line gives it. Searched Walford (whole file, intro l.320-420), Bidez-Parmentier, Photius cod. 29 (Freese l.2410-2416), Gallandi's notice (Migne l.142035-142130). The Walford file header's 'c. 536-c. 594' is a cataloguer's line.

absent_details.detail: His birth year in his own words
absent_details.note: Evagrius gives only that he was a schoolboy at the Apamea display and in his fifty-eighth year when writing IV.29 (walford1846 l.8804-8805, 9044-9045). 'About 536' is Walford's reckoning (l.327-328).

absent_details.detail: Names of his wives and children
absent_details.note: Not given in Walford or Bidez-Parmentier (searched 'wife', 'daughter', 'children' in Walford; l.9038-9046, 11455-11456, 12149-12150).

absent_details.detail: The year of Gregory's hearing at Constantinople
absent_details.note: No held year; Evagrius places it four months before the earthquake of era year 637 (l.11452-11454).

claims.claim: In the 160th year (Brehaut) after Martin, Eufronius's seventh year, Sigibert's second, 'I became ill with malignant pimples and fever, and being unable to eat or drink ... thought of nothing but of the details of my burial'; called on Martin; fell ill again in the forest; friends: 'Let us return home'; he: 'if I have merit to see the holy Martin's church, I shall thank God; but if not, carry my dead body there and bury it, because I am determined not to return home'; 'The third night after arriving at the holy church we planned to keep watch'; after sleeping 'I woke up and found that all weakness and pain were gone'
claims.witness: Gregory, Miracles of Martin I.32, tr. Brehaut (gregory-tours_history-of-the-franks-selections_brehaut1916 l.11570-11619)

claims.claim: The Latin reads 'Anno centesimo sexagesimo tertio post assumtionem sancti ... Martini' (163rd year), with '563' in the margin; Arndt: 'Anno 563. Gregorius Turonis ad tumulum beati Martini profectus' (OCR 'A^ino 563')
claims.witness: Gregory, Mir. Mart. I.32, Latin (gregory-tours_opera-mgh-srm-1-lat_arndt-krusch1885 l.46261-46263, OCR); Arndt's preface (l.766)

claims.claim: Gregory was already a deacon at the time of that journey: 'Illo tempore iam diaconum se ordinatum fuisse, ipse narravit'
claims.witness: Arndt's preface (gregory-tours_opera-mgh-srm-1-lat_arndt-krusch1885 l.479-480, OCR)

claims.claim: 'He was born and grew up at Clermont in Auvergne'
claims.witness: Brehaut's introduction (gregory-tours_history-of-the-franks-selections_brehaut1916 l.85-86, OCR '.Clermont')

claims.claim: Gregory of Langres is 'proavum nostrum': 'secus sanctum Gregorium, proavum nostrum, sepelitur'; Krusch's note: 'S. Gregorius Lingonensis, proavus Gregorii Turonensis ... avus Armentariae, Gregorii nostri matris'
claims.witness: Gregory, History V.5, Latin (gregory-tours_opera-mgh-srm-1-lat_arndt-krusch1885 l.15699-15700, OCR 'sanctura', 'sopelitur'); Krusch's note (l.52425-52426)

claims.claim: Arndt counts Gregory's family 'Inter nobilissimos ergo Romanos in Galliis degentes'; his father Florentius was son of the senator Georgius; his mother Armentaria was of senatorial rank, granddaughter of Gregory of Langres
claims.witness: Arndt's preface (gregory-tours_opera-mgh-srm-1-lat_arndt-krusch1885 l.487-497, OCR)

claims.claim: Birth: 'a. 573. ex. mater sanata, a. 539, aut, si ante mensem Novembrem haec acta sunt, a. 538. Gregorius natus erat', reckoned from his mother's cure after 'triginta quatuor annos' (Mir. Mart. III.10)
claims.witness: Arndt's preface (gregory-tours_opera-mgh-srm-1-lat_arndt-krusch1885 l.447-455, OCR 'viater')

claims.claim: 'Gregory's life covers the years from 538 to 594'
claims.witness: Brehaut's introduction (gregory-tours_history-of-the-franks-selections_brehaut1916 l.81, OCR 'JGlregory'sJife ... 538^0594')

claims.claim: A note in Foulke's translation, in quotation marks, gives: 'was born about 538 at Clermont Ferrand ... became bishop of Tours 573, died 594 or 595'
claims.witness: Foulke's notes to Paul the Deacon (paul-the-deacon_history-of-the-langobards_foulke1907 l.13859-13861); the source of the quoted note is not named in the held lines

claims.claim: 'Anno centesimo septuagesimo secundo post transitum beati Martini antestitis, Sigiberto gloriosissimo rege duodecimo anno regnante, post excessum sancti Eufroni ... onus episcopati indignus accepi', with '573' in the margin; Arndt: consecration 'cum anno tantum 573 convenit'; Arndt: 'Cum hac ratione Gregorius ipse non consentit… Quae computatio annum 569 efficit, qui sine dubio falsus est' (l.410-414); Krusch: 'In calculo sibi minime constat' (l.35416-35418)
claims.witness: Gregory, Mir. Mart. II.1, Latin (gregory-tours_opera-mgh-srm-1-lat_arndt-krusch1885 l.46663-46669, OCR); Arndt's preface (l.391-414); Krusch (l.35416-35418)

claims.claim: Consecration day: Krusch 'Cum autem a. 573, d. 20. Augusti consecratus sit'; Arndt 'Gregorium die 23. mensis eiusdem' from Eufronius's feast on 4 August and the nineteen days' vacancy; Dalton 'Gregory became bishop on the 24th of August'
claims.witness: Krusch's prolegomena (gregory-tours_opera-mgh-srm-1-lat_arndt-krusch1885 l.35333, 35413); Arndt (l.394-396, 407); Dalton's note (gregory-tours_history-of-the-franks-v2_dalton1927 l.22693-22694)

claims.claim: Arndt: 'Veri simile etiam est, Gregorium non a civibus Turonensibus electum, sed a rege intrusum esse'; Monod's other view: 'Quae nunc opinio recta sit, non definio'
claims.witness: Arndt's note (gregory-tours_opera-mgh-srm-1-lat_arndt-krusch1885 l.795-801, OCR)

claims.claim: Fortunatus V.3, 'Ad cives Turonicos de Gregorio episcopo': 'Huic Sigibercthus ovans favet et Brunichildis honori'; 'Martino proprium mittit Iulianus alumnum'
claims.witness: Venantius Fortunatus, Carm. V.3 (venantius-fortunatus_opera-mgh-aa-4-lat_leo-krusch1881 l.10216-10236, OCR rough); quoted cleanly by Arndt (gregory-tours_opera-mgh-srm-1-lat_arndt-krusch1885 l.780-788)

claims.claim: Fortunatus was an Italian poet at Poitiers, a close friend of Gregory, who outlived him and 'vitam posteris tradere neglexit'; 'Venantius ille Fortunatus ... in vicina Pictavensi urbe versabatur ... ex Italia in Gallias adductus'
claims.witness: Arndt's preface (gregory-tours_opera-mgh-srm-1-lat_arndt-krusch1885 l.300-305, 977-980, OCR); MGH AA IV title 'presbyteri Italici' (venantius-fortunatus_opera-mgh-aa-4-lat_leo-krusch1881 l.66)

claims.claim: Chilperic held Tours: 'During these years Chilperic held Tours and the relations between him and Gregory were as a rule unfriendly'
claims.witness: Brehaut's introduction (gregory-tours_history-of-the-franks-selections_brehaut1916 l.416-418)

claims.claim: Chilperic's ordinance that in the Trinity 'we should make no distinction of Persons, but call it only God'; 'This is my will, that such be thy faith'; Gregory: 'know that in their Persons the Father is different from the Son, and the Son from the Holy Ghost'; the king: 'I will set forth these things to others wiser than thou'; Gregory: 'will never be a wise man, but a fool'; 'Thereat he gnashed his teeth, but held his peace'
claims.witness: Gregory, History V.44, tr. Dalton (gregory-tours_history-of-the-franks-v2_dalton1927 l.10361-10398)

claims.claim: Arndt dates the Trinity dispute and the Leudast affair to 580 and calls Chilperic's book 'erroribus Sabellianis infectum'
claims.witness: Arndt's preface (gregory-tours_opera-mgh-srm-1-lat_arndt-krusch1885 l.836-841)

claims.claim: Leudast to the king: 'he saith that thy queen liveth in adultery with Bishop Bertram'; Dalton's note: Leudast was 'Count of Tours'; Arndt: Leudast had been put out of the countship ('Leudastem ex comitatu depulit' (OCR 'pepidit')) before he went to the king
claims.witness: Gregory, History V.47, tr. Dalton (gregory-tours_history-of-the-franks-v2_dalton1927 l.10486-10491, note l.10480); Arndt (gregory-tours_opera-mgh-srm-1-lat_arndt-krusch1885 l.842-851)

claims.claim: 'The bishops assembled at Berny'; Bertram 'questioned me'; 'In all sincerity I denied having said anything of the kind'; 'it was settled that I should say Mass at three altars and clear myself of the accusation by an oath'
claims.witness: Gregory, History V.49, tr. Dalton (gregory-tours_history-of-the-franks-v2_dalton1927 l.10697-10719); the account of the accused party

claims.claim: Brehaut: 'The bishops assembled at Braine'; the Latin 'in synodo apud Brinnacum villam habita' (Arndt)
claims.witness: Brehaut's translation (gregory-tours_history-of-the-franks-selections_brehaut1916 l.6579); Arndt (gregory-tours_opera-mgh-srm-1-lat_arndt-krusch1885 l.857)

claims.claim: Dalton: Fortunatus's poem on the council 'says nothing of the affair mentioned by Gregory'
claims.witness: Dalton's note (gregory-tours_history-of-the-franks-v2_dalton1927 l.27121-27123)

claims.claim: Brehaut: 'we must allow largely for error and prejudice in his statements of fact'; the History is 'often the sole authority' for 'the perishing of the Roman Empire and the beginning of a great modern state'
claims.witness: Brehaut's introduction (gregory-tours_history-of-the-franks-selections_brehaut1916 l.66-73)

claims.claim: Arndt: 'Obiisse Gregorium anno 594, die 17. mensis Novembris, verisimile est'; most necrologies give 17 November; the Tours calendars 'XV. Kal. Decembris sancti Gregorii Turonensis', quoted from Ruinart
claims.witness: Arndt's preface (gregory-tours_opera-mgh-srm-1-lat_arndt-krusch1885 l.967, 1010-1017, OCR 'Ohiisse')

claims.claim: Krusch: 'Gregorius, qui die 17. Novembris colitur, a. 593, Nov. 17. morti occubuisse videtur, neque a. 594, ut alii coniecerunt', from the 21st year of his consecration and the unfinished fourth book of the Miracles of Martin
claims.witness: Krusch's prolegomena (gregory-tours_opera-mgh-srm-1-lat_arndt-krusch1885 l.35412-35437)

claims.claim: 'I adjure all of you, bishops of the Lord, who after me in this my lowliness shall govern the church of Tours ... never to let these books be destroyed or rewritten ... but to leave them all complete and intact in your time just as I myself have left them'
claims.witness: Gregory, History X.31, tr. Dalton (gregory-tours_history-of-the-franks-v2_dalton1927 l.22708-22719)

claims.claim: 'I am fain first to make profession of my own belief, that whoso reads may doubt not that I hold the catholic faith'
claims.witness: Gregory, History I preface, tr. Dalton (gregory-tours_history-of-the-franks-v2_dalton1927 l.338-340)

claims.claim: Paul the Deacon: 'which are written in the books of the reverend man Gregory, bishop of Tours'
claims.witness: Paul the Deacon, History of the Langobards III.1, tr. Foulke (paul-the-deacon_history-of-the-langobards_foulke1907 l.5073-5075)

claims.claim: Arndt rejects the Vita's journey to Rome: 'Quod ante mortem Romam urbem ipsum petiisse ... Vitae scriptor tradit, huic rei fides abrogata est'; the Vita was composed in the tenth century by Odo of Cluny or by clerics of Tours
claims.witness: Arndt's preface (gregory-tours_opera-mgh-srm-1-lat_arndt-krusch1885 l.968-971, 306-308, OCR)

claims.claim: Dalton translates 'proavum nostrum' as 'our ancestor' and his note calls Gregory of Langres 'great-great-grandfather of Gregory of Tours'; Brehaut's introduction: 'his great-grandfather Gregory, bishop of Langres, in honor of whom Gregory discarded the name of Georgius Florentinus'
claims.witness: Dalton (gregory-tours_history-of-the-franks-v2_dalton1927 l.8241-8242, note l.25237-25239); Brehaut (gregory-tours_history-of-the-franks-selections_brehaut1916 l.162-166)

claims.claim: Arndt on the name: 'Num Gregorius tunc demum cognominatus sit, cum sacros ordines suscepit, dubium est'; Dalton prints the rubric 'GEORGIUS FLORENTIUS, OTHERWISE GREGORY, BISHOP OF TOURS'
claims.witness: Arndt's preface (gregory-tours_opera-mgh-srm-1-lat_arndt-krusch1885 l.352-353, OCR); Dalton (gregory-tours_history-of-the-franks-v2_dalton1927 l.226-229)

claims.claim: Book list in X.31: ten books of History, seven of Miracles, one on the Lives of the Fathers, one of commentaries on the Psalms, one on the Offices of the Church
claims.witness: Gregory, History X.31, tr. Dalton (gregory-tours_history-of-the-franks-v2_dalton1927 l.22705-22709)

claims.claim: Krusch on Mir. Mart. IV: 'Gregorium, quominus librum finiret, morte impeditum esse, luce clarius intelligitur'
claims.witness: Krusch's prolegomena (gregory-tours_opera-mgh-srm-1-lat_arndt-krusch1885 l.35412-35414)

claims.claim: Tradition placing: the census lists Gregory of Tours under Merovingian Gallic Christianity
claims.witness: cic-website/data/world-census.json, movements, 'Merovingian Gallic Christianity'

contested_claims.claim: The year of Gregory's death
contested_claims.sides: W. Arndt: 17 November 594, 'verisimile est' (gregory-tours_opera-mgh-srm-1-lat_arndt-krusch1885 l.967); Brehaut: 594 (gregory-tours_history-of-the-franks-selections_brehaut1916 l.81, 431); a quoted note in Foulke: 594 or 595 (paul-the-deacon_history-of-the-langobards_foulke1907 l.13861). Bruno Krusch, in the same volume: 17 November 593, 'neque a. 594, ut alii coniecerunt' (l.35435-35437). No held ancient source gives the year.

contested_claims.claim: The place of the council that tried Gregory
contested_claims.sides: Dalton: Berny (gregory-tours_history-of-the-franks-v2_dalton1927 l.10697; Berny-Riviere, note l.9497). Brehaut: Braine (gregory-tours_history-of-the-franks-selections_brehaut1916 l.6579, note l.12316). The Latin has Brinnacum (gregory-tours_opera-mgh-srm-1-lat_arndt-krusch1885 l.857).

contested_claims.claim: The day of his consecration in 573
contested_claims.sides: Krusch: 20 August (gregory-tours_opera-mgh-srm-1-lat_arndt-krusch1885 l.35333, 35413); Arndt: 23 August, from Eufronius's feast on 4 August and the nineteen days' vacancy (l.392-396, 407); Dalton: 24 August (gregory-tours_history-of-the-franks-v2_dalton1927 l.22693-22694).

contested_claims.claim: How Gregory of Langres was related to him
contested_claims.sides: Gregory's own Latin: 'proavum nostrum' (gregory-tours_opera-mgh-srm-1-lat_arndt-krusch1885 l.15700); Krusch: grandfather of Armentaria, Gregory's mother (l.52425-52426); Brehaut: great-grandfather (gregory-tours_history-of-the-franks-selections_brehaut1916 l.163-164, 5379-5380). Dalton: 'our ancestor' in the text and 'great-great-grandfather' in a note (gregory-tours_history-of-the-franks-v2_dalton1927 l.8242, 25237-25239).

contested_claims.claim: Whether the leading charge at the trial was true
contested_claims.sides: Gregory's own account, the account of the accused party: he denied the words and cleared himself by oath (gregory-tours_history-of-the-franks-v2_dalton1927 l.10700-10719). Leudast's side survives only in Gregory's telling; Riculf's confession under torture is also told by Gregory (l.10775-10782). The one outside witness to the council, Venantius Fortunatus's poem 'Ad Chilpericum regem quando synodus Brinnaco habita est' (Carm. IX.1; venantius-fortunatus_opera-mgh-aa-4-lat_leo-krusch1881 l.17820, OCR), is silent on the charge: Dalton, 'He says nothing of the affair mentioned by Gregory' (gregory-tours_history-of-the-franks-v2_dalton1927 l.27121-27123).

absent_details.detail: An ancient record of the years of his birth and death
absent_details.note: Searched Arndt's and Krusch's prefaces, Dalton, Brehaut, Fortunatus, Fredegar, Paul the Deacon and Loomis. Every year is an editor's reckoning. The Tours calendars, quoted by Arndt from Ruinart, give the day 17 November only (gregory-tours_opera-mgh-srm-1-lat_arndt-krusch1885 l.1013-1017).

Only the tenth-century Vita reports it, through Arndt, who rejects it (gregory-tours_opera-mgh-srm-1-lat_arndt-krusch1885 l.968-971). The Vita, Odo of Cluny's in some manuscripts, is not held (PL 133 has only a notice).
Volume I of Dalton, with his own chronology, is not held; his notes in volume II cite it. Nothing is told from it.
Arndt says Venantius Fortunatus, his friend, left no Life of him (gregory-tours_opera-mgh-srm-1-lat_arndt-krusch1885 l.300-305).

absent_details.detail: The year of the healing at Martin's tomb in Brehaut
absent_details.note: Brehaut's English 'hundred and sixtieth year' (gregory-tours_history-of-the-franks-selections_brehaut1916 l.11571) stands against the Latin 'centesimo sexagesimo tertio' (gregory-tours_opera-mgh-srm-1-lat_arndt-krusch1885 l.46262); the brief gives no year for the scene.

claims.claim: 'Cum essem aliquando apud abbatem Seridum, aegrotare contigit ministrum abbatis Joannis: quare mihi imperavit abbas seniori ut deservirem'; he revered the old man's cell door 'ut qui pretiosam crucem adorat'; each day after his service he bowed and left 'data venia et accepta benedictione'

claims.claim: The abbot John Dorotheus served is John, disciple of Barsanuphius: Dorotheus himself writes 'Memini me quandoque abbatem Joannem beati Barsanuphii discipulum interrogasse' (OCR 'Barsanuplii'); the old man of Doctrina IV §9 is the same 'abbatis Joannis', with no epithet there; Gallandi's notice and the heading of the Questions agree. The epithet 'the Prophet' is the heading's ('ad ejus discipulum abbatem Joannem, cognomento Prophetam') and Gallandi's ('Prophetae titulo clarum'), not Dorotheus's
claims.witness: Dorotheus, Doctrina I, PG 88 (dorotheus-gaza_doctrinae-barsanuphius-climacus-agathias-grc-lat_migne-pg88 l.124096-124098); Doctrina IV §9 (l.126277); Gallandi's Notitia (l.121957-121958); heading of the Questions (l.139574-139581)

claims.witness: PG 88 (dorotheus-gaza_doctrinae-barsanuphius-climacus-agathias-grc-lat_migne-pg88 l.122103-122108, OCR 'Darsanuphii')

contested_claims.claim: When Dorotheus lived
contested_claims.sides: Gallandi reports the Bollandists, Fabricius and Cave for the end of the sixth century and sets aside Oudin, who puts him in the seventh (dorotheus-gaza_doctrinae-barsanuphius-climacus-agathias-grc-lat_migne-pg88 l.121961-121965). Nau: born about 540 (po08 l.11524). Migne's heading: 596 (l.121943). No held ancient source gives a year.

contested_claims.claim: Whether the Dorotheus of the Teachings is the one condemned with the Acephali
contested_claims.sides: The anonymous preface: two of each name, and the Teachings belong to the sound one (dorotheus-gaza_doctrinae-barsanuphius-climacus-agathias-grc-lat_migne-pg88 l.122103-122108); Theodore the Studite separates the condemned from those he accepts (l.122119-122131). Theodore's own profession anathematizes Barsanuphius, Isaiah, Dorotheus and Dositheus 'quos sanctus Sophronius anathematizavit' (PG 99 l.85908-85910). Already a contested claim for batch 3's Barsanuphius and John; no held modern scholar was found discussing it.

contested_claims.claim: Which monastery Dorotheus headed
sides: The Synaxaristes revised by Nikodemos the Hagiorite: after John died he founded a monastery of his own (nikodemos-hagiorite_synaxaristes-vol2-mar-aug-grc_1900 l.37916-37921, OCR very rough)
Nau: the heads in turn of Seridus's monastery were Barsanuphius, Seridus and at last Dorotheus (po08_john-rufus-plerophories-and-others-fra_1912 l.11421-11424)
Gallandi calls him archimandrite without saying of which house (dorotheus-gaza_doctrinae-barsanuphius-climacus-agathias-grc-lat_migne-pg88 l.121957)

absent_details.note: Searched Gallandi's notice, the preface, the letter to a brother, Doctrinae I-IV, XI, the Questions, and the Synaxaristes for 13 August. None gives birthplace, parents or the manner of his death. Gallandi says the death year is not clearly known (dorotheus-gaza_doctrinae-barsanuphius-climacus-agathias-grc-lat_migne-pg88 l.121968-121969).

Not held. Only Gallandi's mention of it (dorotheus-gaza_doctrinae-barsanuphius-climacus-agathias-grc-lat_migne-pg88 l.121958-121960), Dorotheus's own lines on Dositheus (l.123809-123815) and the Synaxaristes memorial are held. Conrad Janning's life in the Acta Sanctorum is not held.

absent_details.detail: An early witness that he founded his own monastery
absent_details.note: The founding is told only by the Synaxaristes revised by Nikodemos the Hagiorite (l.37916-37921), in very rough OCR. Gallandi calls him archimandrite; Nau lists him as the last of the heads of Seridus's monastery (po08 l.11421-11424).
No English translation is held. The brief tells his Latin in modern words and names the source.

claims.claim: On the Sabbath day [Saturday] he and his attendant Diormit go to bless the granary; 'Greatly do I congratulate the monks of my household that this year, also, if I should perchance have to depart from you, you will have enough for the year without stint'; he tells Diormit in secret 'this day is truly a Sabbath day for me' and 'this night, at midnight ... I shall go the way of my fathers'
claims.witness: Adomnán, Life III.23, tr. Huyshe (adomnan huyshe1905 l.10688-10727; '[Saturday]' is Huyshe's bracket)

claims.claim: The white horse that carried the milk pails laid its head on his breast and shed tears; Diormit tried to drive it away; 'Let him alone, let him alone, for he loves me'
claims.witness: Adomnán, Life III.23 (adomnan huyshe1905 l.10735-10760)

claims.claim: Adomnán was ninth abbot of Iona, abbot 679-704, born 624, 'twenty-seven years after the death of Columba'
claims.witness: Huyshe's introduction and notes (adomnan huyshe1905 l.84-88, 1980-1983, 10424-10428)

claims.claim: Adomnán says he writes from 'what we have been able to find was committed to writing before our time' or from 'certain experienced and faithful ancients'
claims.witness: Adomnán, second preface (adomnan huyshe1905 l.2199-2210)

claims.claim: The Life is a saint's Life of prophecies, miracles and visions
claims.witness: Adomnán's three books, tr. Huyshe; the Library's own content note calls it an account of 'Columba's visions and miracles' (adomnan huyshe1905 header l.16-18)

claims.claim: Born of noble parentage; father Fedilmith son of Fergus, mother Aethne
claims.witness: Adomnán, second preface (adomnan huyshe1905 l.2211-2215)

claims.claim: 'In the second year after the battle of Culedrebina (Cooldrevny) and in the forty-second of his age, wishing to make a pilgrimage for Christ from Ireland to Britain, he sailed forth'
claims.witness: Adomnán, second preface (adomnan huyshe1905 l.2219-2224)

claims.claim: Huyshe dates the battle to 561 and the voyage to 563
claims.witness: Huyshe (adomnan huyshe1905 l.536-543, 2272-2276)

claims.claim: Annales Cambriae: 'cxviii. Annus. Columcille in Brittania exiit'
claims.witness: Annales Cambriae, ed. Williams ab Ithel (annales-cambriae williams-ab-ithel1860 l.2417); a tenth-century compilation of earlier entries (header l.2-3), counting by its own years

claims.claim: Bede: 'In the year of our Lord 565 ... there came into Britain a famous priest and abbat ... whose name was Columba'; he came 'in the ninth year of the reign of Bridius'
claims.witness: Bede, HE III.4 (bede giles1903 l.5805-5838); the bracket [A.D. 565.] above is the edition's

claims.claim: Huyshe's note holds the battle the cause of his exile: 'It was the cause of Columba's exile' (l.3026). His introduction is more reserved: 'It was this battle, according to tradition, that led to his exile' (l.542-543); 'The tradition is a constant one that the strife and bloodshed of Cuil Dremhne had something to do with Columba's leaving Ireland' (l.1571-1574); of the tales: 'Such are the legends and traditions which cluster about the exile of Columba. The Old Irish Life says nothing of them', and its account is 'perfectly simple and probable' (l.626-629)

Columba 'was excommunicated by a certain synod for some venial and quite excusable causes — not rightly, as afterwards in the end became clear'; 'This thing was done in Teilte [Teltown, Meath]'; Adomnán does not link it to the battle
claims.witness: Adomnán, Life III.3, tr. Huyshe (adomnan huyshe1905 l.9318-9357; '[Teltown, Meath]' is Huyshe's bracket)

claims.claim: Reeves, as Huyshe reports him: the synod was 'possibly in 561, after the battle of Cul Dreimhne, and Columba's action in bringing about that battle may have been the reason of his excommunication'
claims.witness: Huyshe's note reporting Reeves (adomnan huyshe1905 l.9362-9368); Reeves's edition is not held

claims.claim: King Brude did not open his gates; Columba traced the sign of the Cross, knocked, 'immediately the bolts are violently shot back'; the king came out 'to meet the blessed man with all reverence'
claims.witness: Adomnán, Life II.35 (adomnan huyshe1905 l.7866-7893)

claims.claim: Bede: 'he converted that nation to the faith of Christ, by his preaching and example, whereupon he also received of them the aforesaid island for a monastery'
claims.witness: Bede, HE III.4 (bede giles1903 l.5837-5842)

claims.claim: 'He could not pass the space even of a single hour without applying himself either to prayer, or reading, or writing, or also to some manual labour'
claims.witness: Adomnán, second preface (adomnan huyshe1905 l.2234-2238)

claims.claim: Before he went to Britain he built a monastery in Ireland called Dearm-ach, the Field of Oaks; from both monasteries many others had their beginning through his disciples
claims.witness: Bede, HE III.4 (bede giles1903 l.5849-5856)

claims.claim: The island has for ruler an abbot who is a priest, 'to whose direction all the province, and even the bishops, contrary to the usual method, are subject', after the example of their first teacher, a priest and monk
claims.witness: Bede, HE III.4 (bede giles1903 l.5858-5866)

claims.claim: 'they followed uncertain rules in their observance of the great festival, as having none to bring them the synodal decrees for the observance of Easter'
claims.witness: Bede, HE III.4 (bede giles1903 l.5869-5875); Bede writes from the Roman side of the Easter question

claims.claim: Transcribing the Psalter, he stopped at the verse 'But they that seek the Lord shall not want any good thing': 'what follows let Baithene write'
claims.witness: Adomnán, Life III.23 (adomnan huyshe1905 l.10783-10790)

claims.claim: Last words: 'These my last words I commend to you, O my sons, that ye have mutual and unfeigned charity among yourselves, with peace'
claims.witness: Adomnán, Life III.23 (adomnan huyshe1905 l.10813-10818), Adomnán's report

claims.claim: He died before the altar; Diormit lifted his right hand and he moved it to bless the brethren
claims.witness: Adomnán, Life III.23 (adomnan huyshe1905 l.10855-10880), 'as we have learned from some who were there present'

claims.claim: He died 'at the age of seventy-seven, about thirty-two years after he came into Britain'
claims.witness: Bede, HE III.4 (bede giles1903 l.5846-5849)

claims.claim: 'Forty-five years was he in Scotland, seventy-seven years was his full age'
claims.witness: Book of Lismore Life, tr. Stokes (stokes book-of-lismore 1890 l.17793-17794); a late Middle Irish life

claims.claim: Huyshe's Old Irish Life: 'His age was forty-two when he went. He was thirty-four years in Alba'
claims.witness: Huyshe quoting an Old Irish Life (adomnan huyshe1905 l.641-646)

claims.claim: Reeves: the birthday on 7 December, a Thursday, points to 517 and 523, but 521 is 'most likely to be the true period'
claims.witness: Stokes's note reporting Reeves (stokes book-of-lismore 1890 l.24008-24011); Reeves's edition is not held

claims.claim: The years 521-597 on the title and in the notes
claims.witness: Huyshe (adomnan huyshe1905 l.1, 11204-11208)

claims.claim: Annales Cambriae: 'Lxxvii. Annus. Sanctus Columcille nascitur' and 'CLI. Annus. Columcille moritur'
claims.witness: Annales Cambriae, ed. Williams ab Ithel (annales-cambriae williams-ab-ithel1860 l.2399, 2516)

claims.witness: Editor's margin years (annales-cambriae williams-ab-ithel1860 l.2399, 2417, 2480; the margin column is displaced by OCR, and 595 agrees with the count 118 = 562)
