claims.witness: Huyshe (adomnan huyshe1905 l.849-857); the Irish annals he cites are not held

claims.claim: The blessing of the island was 'one day in the month of May'; his death in the night after the Sabbath
claims.witness: Adomnán, Life III.23 (adomnan huyshe1905 l.10620-10625, 10701-10727)

claims.claim: He died 'when the bell for nocturn was struck on the night of Pentecost Sunday'
claims.witness: Book of Lismore Life (stokes book-of-lismore 1890 l.17947)

claims.claim: Feast of Saints Columba and Baithene, '[June 9]'
claims.witness: Huyshe's bracket and note (adomnan huyshe1905 l.8984-8988, 9057)

claims.claim: His name reached 'even to triangular Spain, and to Gaul, and to Italy ... and also to the city of Rome itself'
claims.witness: Adomnán, quoted by Huyshe (adomnan huyshe1905 l.1855-1866)

claims.claim: At Streaneshalch (Whitby) Colman spoke of 'our most reverend Father Columba'; Wilfrid: 'if that Columba of yours ... was a holy man and powerful in miracles, yet could he be preferred before the most blessed prince of the apostles'
claims.witness: Bede, HE III.25 (bede giles1903 l.8115-8125, 8180-8190); speeches in Bede's telling

claims.claim: The authorship of the Altus Prosator 'is ascribed by an apparently unbroken tradition to Columba, and does not seem open to any serious doubt'
claims.witness: Huyshe reporting the Marquess of Bute (adomnan huyshe1905 l.1698-1703)

contested_claims.claim: The year Columba came to Britain
sides: Huyshe: 563, two years after the battle of Cooldrevny, which he dates to 561 (adomnan huyshe1905 l.536-543, 2272-2276), from Adomnán's 'second year after the battle'
Bede: 565, in the ninth year of Bridius (bede giles1903 l.5805-5838)
Annales Cambriae: their year 118, set by their editor at 562 (williams-ab-ithel1860 l.2417)

contested_claims.claim: His age and years in Britain
sides: Bede: died at seventy-seven, about thirty-two years after coming to Britain (l.5846-5849)
Book of Lismore Life: forty-five years in Scotland, seventy-seven in all (l.17793-17794)
Old Irish Life quoted by Huyshe: forty-two when he went, thirty-four years in Alba (l.641-646); Huyshe's 521-597
Annales Cambriae: birth in their year 77 and death in year 151, set by their editor at 521 and 595 (williams-ab-ithel1860 l.2399, 2516)

contested_claims.claim: Why he left Ireland
sides: Huyshe: his note says the battle of Cooldrevny 'was the cause of Columba's exile' (adomnan huyshe1905 l.3022-3026); his introduction gives it 'according to tradition' (l.542-543), calls the tradition that the battle had something to do with his leaving a constant one (l.1571-1574), counts the tales around the exile as legends (l.626-627) and calls the Old Irish Life's pilgrimage account 'perfectly simple and probable' (l.628-629)
Old Irish Life quoted by Huyshe: a pilgrimage he had determined on from the beginning of his life (l.630-643)

Adomnán: names the battle only to date the voyage (l.2219-2224); tells of a wrongful excommunication at Teltown without naming a cause (l.9318-9357); Reeves, as Huyshe reports him, thinks it possibly over the battle (l.9362-9368)

contested_claims.claim: Who gave him Iona
sides: Bede: the Picts (l.5840-5842)
Irish annals, as Huyshe reports them: Conall, son of Comgill (l.849-857)

contested_claims.claim: The day of his death
sides: Adomnán: the night after a Saturday, after a day in May (l.10620-10727)
Book of Lismore Life: the night of Pentecost Sunday (l.17947)
Huyshe: feast on 9 June (l.8988, 9057)

absent_details.note: No writing of his is held. His sayings are Adomnán's report; the poems and hymns ascribed to him are held only in Huyshe's English of some stanzas.

No Irish annals are held; the Annales Cambriae give birth, voyage and death by their own count of years (williams-ab-ithel1860 l.2399, 2417, 2516), which their editor sets at 521, 562 and 595. 521 and 597 are Huyshe's (521 also Reeves's, through Stokes); Bede gives the age, seventy-seven, and the arrival year 565.
No Annals of Ulster or Tigernach are held; Huyshe's reports of them cannot be checked. Reeves's annotated edition is not held.

claims.claim: Gregory remembers knowing Leander at Constantinople: 'When I knew you long since at Constantinople, my most blessed brother, at the time that I was kept there by the affairs of the Apostolical See, and that you had been brought thither by an embassage, with which you were charged, on counts touching the faith of the Wisigoths'
claims.witness: Gregory the Great, letter to Leander prefixed to the Moralia, Library of the Fathers English (moralia-in-job-books-i-x bliss1844 l.386-390, 452-454; Latin in PL72 l.65286-65305)

claims.claim: The brethren who followed Gregory from his monastery pressed him to set forth the book of Job, 'you too adding your influence, as you yourself remember'
claims.witness: Gregory, letter to Leander (bliss1844 l.640-655); Isidore, De viris illustribus 40, 'efflagitante Leandro episcopo' (PL83 l.122682-122684)

claims.claim: The letter stands at the head of the Moralia ('The Epistle', addressed 'To the Most Devout and Holy Brother, my fellow Bishop Leander'); Barmby: 'The whole, when finished, was addressed to Leander. All this appears from the Epistola Missoria prefixed to the completed treatise'
claims.witness: bliss1844 l.378-387; Barmby's note to Ep. I.43 (npnf212 l.32529-32541)

claims.claim: Leander, son of Severianus of the province of Carthaginiensis, a monk by profession, made from monk bishop of the church of Seville in the province of Baetica; 'vir suavis eloquio, ingenio praestantissimus; vita quoque tantum atque doctrina clarissimus, ut etiam fide ejus atque industria populi gentis Gothorum ab Ariana insania ad fidem catholicam reverterentur'
claims.witness: Isidore of Seville (his younger brother), De viris illustribus ch. 41 (PL83 l.122767-122776; 'cap. 28' in the PL72 Veterum testimonia, l.65250-65259; OCR regularized)

claims.claim: Isidore was Leander's younger brother and succeeded him at Seville
claims.witness: Leander's Rule, 'nec junioris fratris Isidori obliviscaris' (PL72 l.66699-66700); Mommsen, 'Leandri fratris, cui successit' (mommsen1894 l.21985); Ildefonsus, 'Isidorus post Leandrum fratrem' (PL96 l.16899, per dossier); Library of the Fathers note (bliss1844 l.438-440)

claims.claim: 'Hic namque in exsilii sui peregrinatione composuit duos adversus haereticorum dogmata libros'; Isidore gives no place or year for the exile

Leovigild had 'greatly persecuted' Leander, and near death 'commended his son Recharedus ... unto Bishop Leander ... that by his counsel and exhortation, he might likewise make him a member of the Catholic Church'
claims.witness: Gregory the Great, Dialogues III.31, English of 1608 ed. Gardner (dialogues gardner1911 l.8073-8080)

claims.claim: Altamira argued 'there is no evidence in contemporary documents to prove' that Leovigild commanded Leander to convert Recared
claims.witness: O. M. Dalton's note to Gregory of Tours VIII.46 (dalton1927 l.29043-29047)

claims.claim: Gregory learned 'of many which came from Spain' that Hermenegild 'was from Arian heresy lately converted to the Catholic faith by the most reverent man Leander, Bishop of Seville, with whom I was not long since familiarly acquainted'
claims.witness: Gregory the Great, Dialogues III.31 (gardner1911 l.8012-8017)

claims.claim: Ingund 'began to enjoin upon her lord that he should forsake the errors of his heresy'; he 'was moved at length by her exhortation; he was converted to the Catholic law'
claims.witness: Gregory of Tours, History V.38, tr. Dalton (dalton1927 l.9975-9978, 9993-9995)

claims.claim: Dalton: Hermangild 'was probably converted through the influence of Ingund, and by the teaching of Leander'; neither Isidore nor John of Biclar records the conversion; after it Leander withdrew to Constantinople
claims.witness: Dalton's note (dalton1927 l.26920-26928)

claims.claim: Dalton calls Gregory the Great's account of Hermenegild's martyrdom 'fictitious' and suggests 'Perhaps he derived his supposed facts from his friend Leander'; Leander 'dared not return to Spain until the death of Leuvigild'
claims.witness: Dalton's note (dalton1927 l.28849-28854); also l.29205-29208

claims.claim: At the Third Council of Toledo 'summa tamen synodalis negotii penes sanctum Leandrum Hispalensis ecclesiae episcopum et beatissimum Eutropium monasterii Servitani abbatem fuit'
claims.witness: John of Biclaro, Chronicle, Maurice VIII / Reccared IV, Mommsen margin '590?' (mommsen1894 l.20388-20399; PL72 l.65088-65091)

claims.claim: The council met in Reccared's fourth year, 'die viii iduum majarum era DCXXVII' (OCR 'viri', 'pcxxvir'); 589 is the year James Barmby and Henry Percival give
claims.witness: Toledo III acts (collectio 1808 l.36599-36601); Barmby (npnf212 l.32578-32584 note); Percival (npnf214 l.13698)

claims.claim: Leander signed: 'Leander in Christi nomine ecclesiae catholicae Hispalensis metropolitanus episcopus provinciae Baeticae his constitutionibus, quibus in urbe Toletana interfui, annuens subscripsi'
claims.witness: Toledo III acts (collectio 1808 l.38055-38063)

claims.claim: Homily headed 'Homilia Sancti Leandri in laudem ecclesiae ob conversionem gentis post concilium et confirmationem canonum edita'; opens 'Festivitatem hanc omnium esse solemniorem festivitatum novitas ipsa significat, quoniam sicut nova est conversio tantarum plebium causa'; 'repente novos ecclesiam parturisse populos intuemur, et quorum asperitatem quondam gemebamus, de eorum nunc gaudemus credulitate'; ends praying 'ut regnum et gens, quae Christum glorificavit in terris, glorificetur ab illo non solum in terris sed etiam in coelis'
claims.witness: collectio 1808 l.38309-38333, 38601-38607 (OCR 'hancomnium', 'comversionem'); reprinted PL72 l.66746-66760

claims.claim: The 1808 editors: 'Deest haec homilia in A. et E. 3. desumpta est ex codice BR. cum variantibus reliquorum lectionibus'
claims.witness: collectio 1808 footnote 61 (l.38343, 38415)

claims.claim: Isidore lists among his works 'unum ad Florentinam sororem de Institutione virginum et contemptu mundi libellum, titulorum distinctionibus praenotatum'

Rule opens 'Perquirenti mihi, soror charissima Florentina, quibus te divitiarum cumulis haeredem facerem'; gold and silver are of the earth and return to it; 'Quidquid enim sub sole conspexi, nihil te dignum, sorore [sic], arbitratus sum'; Christ 'Sponsus est, frater est, amicus est, pars haereditatis est'
claims.witness: Leander, Regula (PL72 l.65370-65386, 65413-65414; OCR regularized)

claims.claim: Florentina has made a pact with Christ: 'si pactum quod cum Christo pepigisti servaveris'; chapter XXI 'Ne velit virgo reverti ad Saeculum', 'cum uxore Loth non respicias retro'
claims.witness: Regula (PL72 l.66662-66674, 66712-66714; OCR regularized)

claims.claim: 'nec junioris fratris Isidori obliviscaris: quem quia sub Dei tuitione, et tribus germanis superstitibus parentes reliquerunt communes, laeti, et de ejus nihil formidantes infantia, ad Dominum commearunt'
claims.witness: Regula ch. XXI (PL72 l.66699-66702; OCR 'Isidoii obhviscaris', regularized)

claims.claim: Gregory to Leander: 'even though absent in the body, I behold thee always present with me; for I carry the image of thy countenance stamped within the bowels of my heart'; Turchi dates the letter (I.41; Barmby I.43) to April 591; Barmby gives 591 'if rightly placed'
claims.witness: Gregory, Register I.43, tr. Barmby (npnf212 l.32623-32627); Turchi (turchi1907 l.9918-9925)

claims.claim: Gregory sends Leander 'a pallium, to be used only in celebration of Mass'; 'Your Holiness writes of being afflicted with the pains of gout, by continual suffering from which I too am grievously worn down'; Ludwig M. Hartmann (editing after Paul Ewald's death) dates IX.227 to August 599
claims.witness: Gregory, Register IX.121, tr. Barmby (npnf213 l.3830-3839); Hartmann's heading (ewald-hartmann1893 l.15112-15115, OCR '5!HI, Aug.'; running head l.15345)

claims.claim: Isidore: 'Floruit sub Reccaredo, viro religioso ac principe glorioso, cujus etiam temporibus mirabili obitu actualis vitae terminum clausit'
claims.witness: Isidore, DVI 41 as printed in the PL72 testimonia (PL72 l.65267-65269, OCR regularized); PL83 l.122809-122812 (column-broken)

claims.claim: Epitaph 'Crux haec alma': 'Obiit felicis memoriae Leander episcopus die III Kalend. Martias, aera DCXLI'; Mommsen reckons 27 Feb 603 and writes 'ei epitaphio codicibus nescio quibus propagato quatenus fides habenda sit, nescio'; the PL96 editor holds the poem 'neque Hildefonsi, nec alterius antiqui'
claims.witness: PL72 l.66726-66740 (OCR 'Ohiit felicis memoi ix'); Mommsen (mommsen1894 l.21985-21987); PL96 l.2083-2090

claims.claim: Death year given variously: 603 (PL72 Observatio critica, 'ad annum 603', l.65363); 600 or 601 (Turchi, 'ab an. circ. 584 ad an. 600 vel 601', turchi1907 l.2440-2442); 600 (note signed PER[EZ] in PL83, 'Ego Leandrum anno Christi 600 mortuum colligo', l.122864-122870); 599 (Gardner, 'St. Leander died in 599', gardner1911 l.13056-13057); 595 (Library of the Fathers note, 'He died in 595', bliss1844 l.420-421)
claims.witness: as cited

claims.claim: John of Biclaro: 'Leander Hispalensis ecclesiae episcopus clarus habetur', in the year-block of Maurice III / Leovigild XVII, which Mommsen's margin gives as '585?'

Cave's notice (PL72, headed 'NOTITIA. (Ex Cave.)'): Leander went as envoy to the emperor Tiberius at Constantinople 'ut suppetias obtineret', after Leovigild's armed persecution of Hermenegild, and formed friendship with Gregory, then deacon and apocrisiarius; back in Spain, 'anno 384' (OCR-damaged), exiled by Leovigild; the year after, Leovigild commended Reccared to him; 'adeo ut Gothorum apostolus dici meruerit'
claims.witness: William Cave, reprinted by Migne (PL72 l.65123-65160)

claims.claim: Library of the Fathers note: Baronius says Leander went on an embassy to ask help for Hermenegild from the emperor; an ancient Roman Breviary says he went to Constantinople to attend a council 'Pro confirmandis capitulis Sanctae Trinitatis'; he 'took part (and perhaps presided, see Baronius ...) in the third Council of Toledo'

Toledo IV quotes Gregory's answer to Leander: 'efflagitante sanctissimo Leandro episcopo de hac Hispaniae diversitate quid potius esset sequendum, inter cetera rescribens ei sic ait: De trina vero mersione baptismatis ...'; Mommsen dates Toledo IV to 633
claims.witness: collectio 1808 l.38918-38932; Mommsen (mommsen1894 l.21965)

claims.claim: Roman Martyrology, 27 February: 'Hispali in Hispania natalis sancti Leandri ejusdem civitatis episcopi, cujus praedicatione et industria Wisigothorum gens, adjuvante Reccaredo eorum rege, ab Ariana impietate ad catholicam fidem conversa est'
claims.witness: quoted in the PL72 testimonia (PL72 l.65235-65242)

claims.claim: Leander as brother of Leovigild's first wife and uncle of Hermenegild and Reccared appears in Lucas of Tuy's insertion into Isidore's History ('Theodosiam filiam Severiani ducis Carthaginensis ... ex qua Hermegildum et Reccaredum filios suscepit L'), in the breviary Elogium the Bollandists print ('Reccaredum ... filios sororis suae'), and in Gardner's note
claims.witness: mommsen1894 apparatus l.28133-28134; Acta Sanctorum Junii V (palme1867 l.6196-6206); gardner1911 l.13047-13050

claims.claim: Leander lines in Isidore's History of the Goths (preaching to Hermenegild, recall from exile, the friendship with Gregory) are insertions of later manuscripts and of Lucas of Tuy (siglum L), recorded in Mommsen's apparatus; PL83's text of the History has no Leander

contested_claims.claim: The year of Leander's death
contested_claims.sides: Epitaph: era 641, 27 Feb 603 in Mommsen's reckoning, which Mommsen doubts (PL72 l.66739-66740; mommsen1894 l.21985-21987); PL72 Observatio critica: 603 (l.65363). Turchi: 600 or 601 (turchi1907 l.2440-2442). Perez in PL83: 600 (l.122864-122870). Gardner: 599 (gardner1911 l.13057). Library of the Fathers note: 595 (bliss1844 l.420-421), against Gregory's letter IX.227 dated August 599 by Ludwig M. Hartmann (l.15112-15115). Isidore: in Reccared's time (PL72 l.65267-65269).

contested_claims.claim: Who turned Hermenegild to the Catholic faith
contested_claims.sides: Gregory the Great: Leander (gardner1911 l.8012-8017). Gregory of Tours: Ingund's urging (dalton1927 l.9975-9995). Dalton: probably both (l.26920-26922).

contested_claims.claim: Whether Leovigild entrusted Reccared to Leander
contested_claims.sides: Gregory the Great, Dialogues III.31 (gardner1911 l.8073-8080) and Cave after him (PL72 l.65151-65153). Altamira, reported by Dalton: no evidence in contemporary documents (dalton1927 l.29043-29047).

contested_claims.claim: The exile: when, and whether Leander was exiled after Constantinople or withdrew there
contested_claims.sides: Isidore: books written in exile abroad, no place or date (PL83 l.122776-122778). Cave: exiled by Leovigild after returning from Constantinople, year OCR-damaged (PL72 l.65149-65151); Turchi: exiled by Leovigild for Hermenegild's conversion, no year given (turchi1907 l.2438-2443; his 'about 584' is the start of Leander's years as bishop, l.2436, 2446). Dalton: withdrew to Constantinople to escape Leovigild and returned only after his death (dalton1927 l.26925-26926, 28853-28854, 29205-29208).

contested_claims.claim: Whether Leander was Reccared's uncle
contested_claims.sides: Late tradition says so: Lucas of Tuy's insertion (mommsen1894 l.28133-28134), the breviary Elogium (Acta Sanctorum Junii V l.6196-6206), Gardner (gardner1911 l.13047-13050). Isidore (DVI 41), John of Biclaro, Gregory the Great and Gregory of Tours do not say it.

contested_claims.claim: Whether Leander presided at Toledo III
contested_claims.sides: John of Biclaro: the council's business lay with Leander and Eutropius (mommsen1894 l.20398-20399). Library of the Fathers note: 'perhaps presided', citing Baronius (bliss1844 l.413-416). The acts name no president; his signature comes after those of the king, Masona and Euphemius (collectio 1808 l.38029-38063).

absent_details.note: No source used here gives it. The PL72 file header gives 'c. 534-600' as a catalogue date; no held line supports it.

absent_details.detail: The place and date of his exile
absent_details.note: Isidore gives neither (PL83 l.122776-122778). Cave's year is OCR-damaged ('anno 384', PL72 l.65149); Turchi gives no year for the exile (turchi1907 l.2438-2443). Searched PL72, PL83, Mommsen's Biclaro and Isidore, the Toledo acts, Gregory's letters (Barmby, Turchi, Hartmann), Dalton, Gardner, Library of the Fathers notes.

The census rows cite the Rule at PL72 l.65842-65843, which carries no date. The only held 579 near Leander is the OCR-damaged start year in the Observatio critica ('ab anno t>7a ad annum 603', PL72 l.65363). Mommsen's margin '579?' (mommsen1894 l.20108) is for Hermenegild's revolt, not Leander.

absent_details.detail: An English translation of the Rule, the homily or De viris illustribus 41
absent_details.note: None held. The brief's tellings of the Rule and homily are paraphrases of the Latin.

absent_details.detail: His two books against the heretics, the work against Arian customs, and his letters
absent_details.note: Isidore lists them (PL83 l.122776-122809); Cave says they are lost (PL72 l.65165-65170). None is held.
Cave names her Turtura (PL72 l.65129, OCR 'Turturaj'). The Rule's 'quae turture matre nata es' (PL72 l.66688-66692) may play on the name or figure the abbess. Not used in the brief or card.

claims.claim: Fortunatus and Felix suffered 'a very grievous disease of the eyes'; 'they both proceeded to the church of the blessed Paul and John, which is situated within that city, and in which an altar, built in honor of St. Martin the Confessor, has a window near by in which a lamp was set to give light'; they touched their eyes with its oil; 'Instantly the disease was driven away'
claims.witness: Paul the Deacon, History of the Langobards II.13, tr. Foulke (paul-the-deacon foulke1907 l.4082-4091)

claims.claim: Felix was bishop of the church of Tarvisium (Treviso); Fortunatus 'had declared that this Felix was his colleague'
claims.witness: Paul II.13 (paul-the-deacon foulke1907 l.4050-4069)

claims.claim: Fortunatus's own verse: 'inlustrem socium Felicem quaeso require, / cui mecum lumen Martinus reddidit olim' and 'iam desperatum lumen niihi [OCR mihi] reddidit auctor'; 'est ulji [OCR ubi] basilicae culmeu Pauli atque lohaunis'
claims.witness: Fortunatus, Vita Martini IV (venantius-fortunatus leo-krusch1881 l.31286-31327)

claims.claim: Gregory's account, from Fortunatus: at Ravenna the light was restored to him and to 'socii sui Felicis' 'ex oleo, quod sub imagine picturae beati Martini in cicendile ardebat'
claims.witness: Gregory of Tours, De virtutibus S. Martini I.15 (gregory-tours arndt-krusch1885 l.46118-46120); kept on the card, not in the brief

claims.claim: Paul took the birthplace, the healing of the eyes at Ravenna and the journey to Tours from Fortunatus's Vita Martini IV
claims.witness: Foulke's note, citing R. Jacobi's 1877 study of Paul's sources ('(Jacobi, 27, 28)'; paul-the-deacon foulke1907 l.15709-15722; Jacobi's study named in Foulke's preface l.174-177); Jacobi's finding, reported by Foulke

claims.claim: Born 'in a place which is called Duplabilis, which place lies not far from the fortress of Ceneta (Ceneda) and the city of Tarvisium (Treviso)'; 'brought up and instructed at Ravenna' in 'the grammatical, the rhetorical and also the metrical art'
claims.witness: Paul II.13 (paul-the-deacon foulke1907 l.4074-4081); his own verse 'per Cenetam gradieus [OCR] et amicos Duplavenenses' (venantius-fortunatus leo-krusch1881 l.31289)

claims.claim: 'Fortunatus adored the blessed Martin so much that he abandoned his country a little before the Langobards invaded Italy, and set out for the sepulchre of that blessed man at Turones (Tours)'
claims.witness: Paul II.13 (paul-the-deacon foulke1907 l.4091-4095)

claims.claim: Krusch: 'haud multo postquam a. 565 in Gallias venit' (his coming to Gaul in 565)
claims.witness: Krusch, Proemium (venantius-fortunatus leo-krusch1881 l.41198-41199)

claims.claim: Leo's index: summoned from Italy by King Sigibert, between the year Sigibert succeeded his father and 567 (OCR damaged: 'inter ii. 50/, quo Sigi- htrethiu palri tueettiit, el 567'); read as 561-567
claims.witness: Leo, Index personarum (venantius-fortunatus leo-krusch1881 l.51727-51733)

claims.claim: 'after he had come to Turones (Tours), according to his own vow, passing on through Pictavi (Poitiers), he dwelt there and wrote at that place of the doings of many saints, part in prose and part in metrical fashion'
claims.witness: Paul II.13 (paul-the-deacon foulke1907 l.4110-4113)

claims.claim: Radegund, queen of the Thuringians, taken and married by Chlothar I, withdrew to the monastery of the Holy Cross at Poitiers, 'ibi Fortunato familiariter usa est'
claims.witness: Krusch, Proemium (venantius-fortunatus leo-krusch1881 l.41893-41897); Gregory HF IX.40 for her founding the monastery (gregory-tours dalton1927 l.19598-19599)

claims.claim: To Agnes: 'Matcr lionore iiiilii , soror aiitciu diilcis aiiiorc' [OCR: Mater honore mihi, soror autem dulcis amore]; 'caclesti aftcctu , iion criniine corporis ullo: nou caro , scd lioc quod s|)iritas optat aino. tcstis adest Cliristus' [OCR: caelesti affectu, non crimine corporis ullo: non caro, sed hoc quod spiritus optat amo. testis adest Christus]
claims.witness: Fortunatus, Carm. XI.6 (venantius-fortunatus leo-krusch1881 l.22363-22369)

claims.claim: Agnes was abbess of the monastery of the Holy Cross: Carm. XI.5 is headed to the abbess ('ad abbatissam', OCR 'ail ahliatissain') and names 'Agnes' (OCR 'Afjncs'); Leo's index lists his poems to Agnes
claims.witness: Fortunatus, Carm. XI.5 (venantius-fortunatus leo-krusch1881 l.22331-22334); Leo, Index personarum (venantius-fortunatus leo-krusch1881 l.50812-50816)

claims.claim: Poems for kings (Sigibert, Chilperic and his sons) and bishops; prose Lives of Hilary, Germanus, Albinus, Paternus, Radegund, Marcellus
claims.witness: Leo's index (venantius-fortunatus leo-krusch1881 l.51727-51760); Krusch, Proemium (venantius-fortunatus leo-krusch1881 l.41085-42900)

claims.claim: Martin's life in four books of verse: 'Fortunatus presbitcr omne opus vitac eius in quattuor libris vcrsu conscripsit'; Paul: 'Here he wrote the life of St. Martin in four books in heroic meter'
claims.witness: Gregory, Virt. Mart. I.2 (gregory-tours arndt-krusch1885 l.45245-45246); Paul II.13 (paul-the-deacon foulke1907 l.4117-4118)

claims.claim: Gregory: 'quod venerabilcm conservum meum Fortuna- tuni presbiteriim relulisse commemoro' [OCR: venerabilem conservum meum Fortunatum presbiterum]
claims.witness: Gregory, Virt. Mart. I.13, as quoted in Leo's index (venantius-fortunatus leo-krusch1881 l.51804-51806; scrambled OCR in gregory-tours arndt-krusch1885 l.46086)

claims.claim: Gregory, in a dream-dialogue with his mother: 'Utinam Severus aut Paulinus viverent, aut certe Fortunatus adesset, qui ista discriberent!'
claims.witness: Gregory, Virt. Mart. I prol. (gregory-tours arndt-krusch1885 l.45001-45004)

claims.claim: Dalton: the fragment of the True Cross sent to Radegund, 'the arrival of which at Poitiers was celebrated by Fortunatus in several hymns; of which the most familiar begin with the lines Pange lingua gloriosi praelium certaminis, and Vexilla Regis prodeunt'
claims.witness: Dalton's note (gregory-tours dalton1927 l.27596-27600; also l.29581-29583)

claims.claim: 'Vexilla Regis prodeunt , / Fulget crucis mysterium'; heading 'Hymnus ejusdem. Fortunati de éruce [OCR cruce] Salvatoris nostri Jesu Christi'; the brief's 'the banners of the King go forward' is the narrator's plain telling
claims.witness: Hymn printed in Alcuin's works, PL 101 (alcuin pl100-101 migne1863 l.110230-110238); Leo's edition, Carm. II.6, OCR rough (venantius-fortunatus leo-krusch1881 l.4419-4424)

claims.claim: Paul: 'he composed many other things, most of all hymns for particular festivals and especially little verses to particular friends, being second to none of the poets in soft and fluent speech'
claims.witness: Paul II.13 (paul-the-deacon foulke1907 l.4118-4121)

claims.claim: 'lastly in the same city he was ordained, first as a presbyter and then as a bishop, and in the same place he reposes buried with befitting honor'
claims.witness: Paul II.13 (paul-the-deacon foulke1907 l.4113-4116)

claims.claim: 'vir apostolicus Fortunatus episcopus'
claims.witness: Baudonivia, Life of Radegund II, prologue (fredegar ... mgh-srm-2 krusch1888 l.29493)

claims.claim: Gregory calls him presbyter in HF V.8 ('the book of his Life composed by the priest Fortunatus'), Glory of the Martyrs 41 ('Fortunatus presbiter'), Virt. Mart. I.2 and I.13, and Gl. Conf. 44 ('a Fortunato presbytero conscriptam'); the prologue to Virt. Mart. I names him with no title ('aut certe Fortunatus adesset', gregory-tours arndt-krusch1885 l.45002-45003)
claims.witness: gregory-tours dalton1927 l.8393-8394; gregory-tours arndt-krusch1885 l.39955 (Gl. Mart. 41), l.45245 (Virt. Mart. I.2), l.46089-46090 (Virt. Mart. I.13; OCR rough), l.58768 (Gl. Conf. 44, OCR 'pvcsbitero'), quoted by the editors at l.35573; the one 'Fortunatus Pictavensis episcopus' in gregory-tours arndt-krusch1885 (l.328) is a codex lemma the editors call false

claims.claim: Dalton: 'Gregory never alludes to Fortunatus as bishop, because the latter was only consecrated to the see of Poitiers after his death (cf. Introduction, p. 83 n. i)'; the Introduction is not held; Dalton is Gregory's English translator, and the brief gives his view as what he thinks, not as fact
claims.witness: Dalton's note (gregory-tours dalton1927 l.26296-26299)

claims.claim: Luchi: Gregory calls him only presbyter because Fortunatus was made bishop of Poitiers only at the end of his life, when Gregory had died; 'Qiio vero aiiiio Forlunaius sedem Piciavien- sein consceiiilcrii, diflicile est defiiiire' [OCR: Quo vero anno Fortunatus sedem Pictaviensem conscenderit, difficile est definire]
claims.witness: Luchi (regula-magistri-cresconius pl88 migne1862 (Luchi's Vita) l.2916-2927)

claims.claim: An unsigned note answers 'eos qui Foiiuna- tum es albo Pictavensium pontiflcum espunsunt' [OCR], citing Paul and 'Baudonivia Fortunato aequahs'
claims.witness: Note to the Life of Radegund, PL 72 (john-biclaro-leander pl72 migne1878 l.50772-50776)

claims.claim: Born about 530, died about 600
claims.witness: Foulke's note (paul-the-deacon foulke1907 l.15718-15720)

claims.claim: Luchi reports the common belief that he was born about 530 ('natus crediiur circ:i annum 530' [OCR: natus creditur circa annum 530], 'is believed to have been born'); died old at Poitiers early in the seventh century
claims.witness: Luchi (regula-magistri-cresconius pl88 migne1862 (Luchi's Vita) l.1101-1103)

claims.claim: 'Venantius Fortunatus, bishop of Poictiers, who died about 609'
claims.witness: Hugh Williams's note (gildas williams1899 l.12820)

claims.claim: Foulke: 'He was the author of 600 hymns'
claims.witness: Foulke's note (paul-the-deacon foulke1907 l.15719-15720); no held source behind the count

claims.claim: Paul at the tomb: 'At his grave, when I came thither for the purpose of prayer, upon the request of Aper the abbot of that place I composed this epitaph'; the epitaph includes 'Famous in talent, quick to perceive and in speech ever gentle.'
claims.witness: Paul II.13, tr. Foulke (paul-the-deacon foulke1907 l.4122-4129); Foulke dates the visit 782-786 after Waitz (l.4145)

claims.claim: Epitaph 'Epitaphium Fortunati poete Christiani': 'presul requiescit ... Fortunatus enim vir, decus Ecclesiz [OCR Ecclesiae], Plurima qui fecit sanctorum carmina metro'
claims.witness: Poem XCVI in Alcuin's works, PL 101 (alcuin pl100-101 migne1863 l.59551-59559); authorship not stated in the lines read

claims.claim: Krusch denies him the Life of Medard ('utruni Fortunati fucrit annon quacstio inanis cst' [OCR], of an older lost Life); Arndt and Krusch call the short Life of Remigius 'Fortunato male tributa'; Krusch rejects Tillemont's giving the Life of Marcellus to a Fortunatus of Vercelli
claims.witness: venantius-fortunatus leo-krusch1881 l.42459-42550, 42157-42175; gregory-tours arndt-krusch1885 l.60195-60196; Krusch, SRM 3 (passiones-vitaeque-sanctorum-merovingici krusch1896 l.19288-19293)

claims.claim: Full name 'VENANTI HONORI CLEMENTIANI FORTVNATI PRESBYTERI ITALICI'
claims.witness: MGH title page (venantius-fortunatus leo-krusch1881 l.64-66); Leo's index (venantius-fortunatus leo-krusch1881 l.51717-51720)

contested_claims.claim: Whether and when he was bishop of Poitiers
sides: Paul the Deacon: ordained priest and then bishop at Poitiers (paul-the-deacon foulke1907 l.4113-4116); Baudonivia: 'vir apostolicus Fortunatus episcopus' (fredegar ... mgh-srm-2 krusch1888 l.29493); an unsigned PL 72 note uses both against those who struck him from the list (pl72 l.50772-50776)

Gregory of Tours calls him presbyter (gregory-tours dalton1927 l.8393-8394; gregory-tours arndt-krusch1885 l.45245, 35573); Dalton (gregory-tours dalton1927 l.26296-26299) and Luchi (regula-magistri-cresconius pl88 migne1862 (Luchi's Vita) l.2916-2927) explain this by a consecration after Gregory's death; no held source gives the year

contested_claims.claim: Where at Ravenna the healing oil burned
sides: Paul: a lamp in a window near an altar of Martin in the church of Paul and John (paul-the-deacon foulke1907 l.4085-4089)
Gregory, from Fortunatus: a lamp beneath a painted image of Martin (gregory-tours arndt-krusch1885 l.46118-46119)
Fortunatus's poem names the church of Paul and John and an image of the saint on its wall, and Martin's 'loculum' ({leo} l.31322-31328)

contested_claims.claim: His years
sides: Foulke: about 530 to about 600 (paul-the-deacon foulke1907 l.15718-15720)
Luchi: born about 530, died early in the seventh century (regula-magistri-cresconius pl88 migne1862 (Luchi's Vita) l.1101-1103)
Hugh Williams: died about 609 (gildas williams1899 l.12820)

Coming to Gaul: Krusch 565 (venantius-fortunatus leo-krusch1881 l.41199); Leo's index between 561 and 567 (venantius-fortunatus leo-krusch1881 l.51727-51733); Paul: a little before the Lombards invaded (paul-the-deacon foulke1907 l.4091-4093)

contested_claims.claim: Which prose Lives are his
sides: Earlier scholars gave him the Life of Medard: Krusch quotes the codex clause 'Fortunatus pruesbitcr cim- piisuit hucc vita vcl actus sancti Mcdunli' [OCR: Fortunatus presbiter composuit haec vita vel actus sancti Medardi] and two Soissons monks (venantius-fortunatus leo-krusch1881 l.42457-42468); Tillemont gave the Life of Marcellus to an older Fortunatus (venantius-fortunatus leo-krusch1881 l.41188-41193)

Krusch: the extant Life of Medard was written after 602 ('post a. dcniuin (1(12' [OCR: post a. demum 602]) and is not his, and whether the older lost book was his is 'quaestio inanis'; the Life of Marcellus is the poet's (venantius-fortunatus leo-krusch1881 l.42540-42550, 41192-41193); Arndt and Krusch: the short Life of Remigius is 'Fortunato male tributa' (gregory-tours arndt-krusch1885 l.60195-60196)

absent_details.detail: Any year of his life in an ancient source
absent_details.note: Searched Paul II.13, every Fortunatus mention in Gregory (Dalton and Arndt-Krusch), Baudonivia, Leo's index entry, Krusch's Proemium and Luchi's Vita. All years are modern reckonings.
Paul and Baudonivia call him bishop without a year; Luchi says the year is hard to fix; Dalton's Introduction, which he cites, is not held.

absent_details.detail: An English translation of his hymns
absent_details.note: Searched all files for 'royal banners', 'banners of the King', 'Sing, my tongue' and English 'Vexilla'. None held; the Latin is in Leo's edition and in PL 101. The brief gives the first line in Latin with a plain modern telling.

Gregory reports Fortunatus said his father was healed by a remedy of Martin, without a name (gregory-tours arndt-krusch1885 l.46103-46104); his poem names a sister Titiana (venantius-fortunatus leo-krusch1881 l.22374); nothing names father or mother.
Fortunatus of Grado, Fortunatus of Naples, Fortunatus of Fano and the martyr Fortunatus of Aquileia are other men; the Felix of the healing is Felix of Treviso, not Felix of Nantes.

claims.claim: After the three-day fast, on 'die octavo iduum majarum', 'ecce in medio eorum adfuit serenissimus princeps, seque cum Dei sacerdotibus orationi communicans ... sic ad loquendum exorsus est'
claims.witness: Toledo III acts (collectio-canonum-ecclesiae-hispanae 1808 l.36614-36620)

claims.claim: The king: 'non multos post discessus genitoris nostri dies quibus nos vestra beatitudo fidei catholicae sanctae cognovit esse sociatos'; what he had to say of his faith is 'in hunc tomum conscripta', to be read 'in medio vestri'
claims.witness: Toledo III acts (l.36620-36630)

claims.claim: 'Susceptus est autem ab omnibus Dei sacerdotibus offerente rege sacrosanctae fidei tomus, et pronuntiante notario clara voce recensitus est'
claims.witness: Toledo III acts (l.36631-36632)

claims.claim: The council is dated 'anno regnante quarto ... domino Recaredo rege, die viii iduum majarum era DCXXVII' (OCR 'viri', 'pcxxvir'); 589 is the year James Barmby and Henry Percival give
claims.witness: acts l.36598-36600; Barmby (npnf212 l.32578-32584 note; npnf213 l.3852-3856); Percival (npnf214 l.13698)

claims.claim: Tomus: 'Quamvis Deus omnipotens pro utilitatibus populorum regni nos culmen subire tribuerit, et moderamen gentium non paucarum regiae nostrae curae commiserit, meminimus tamen nos mortalium conditione praestringi'

Tomus confesses the Father who begot the Son 'ex sua substantia ... coaequalem et coaeternum', and the Holy Spirit 'a Patre et Filio procedere et cum Patre et Filio unius esse substantiae'; it receives the four councils

Tomus: 'me quoque, ut re ipsa conspicitis calore fidei accensum in eo Dominus excitavit, ut ... populum, qui sub nomine religionis famulabatur errori, ad agnitionem fidei et ecclesiae catholicae consortium revocarem. Adest enim omnis gens Gothorum inclyta'; 'Nec enim sola Gothorum conversio ad cumulum nostrae mercedis accessit, quinimmo et Suevorum gentis infinita multitudo, quam praesidio coelesti nostro regno subjecimus ... ad veritatis originem studio revocavimus' (the Goths are said to be present; the Sueves' conversion is added, not their presence); 'has nobilissimas gentes ... quasi sanctum et placabile sacrificium per vestras manus aeterno Deo offero'
Tomus: 'anathematizo Arium cum omnibus dogmatibus et complicibus suis'

Subscription: 'Ego Recaredus rex fidem hanc sanctam et veram confessionem, quam una per totum orbem catholica confitetur ecclesia; corde retinens, ore affirmans, mea dextera Deo protegente subscripsi'; then 'Ego Baddo gloriosa regina hanc fidem quam credidi et suscepi, mea manu de toto corde subscripsi'
Acclamation: 'Cui a Deo aeternum meritum nisi vero catholico Recaredo regi? Cui a Deo aeterna corona nisi vero orthodoxo Recaredo regi?'
Edict signed 'Flavius Recaredus rex hanc deliberationem quam cum sancta definivimus synodo confirmans subscripsi'; what was defined 'nulli contemnere liceat, nullus praeterire praesumat'

Canon II in Percival's English: 'the holy Synod enacts, with the advice of our most pious and most glorious Lord, King Recarede, that through all the churches of Spain and Gallæcia, the symbol of faith of the council of Constantinople ... should be recited according to the form of the Eastern Church'
claims.witness: Henry R. Percival, Excursus (npnf214 l.13736-13742)

claims.claim: Dalton: 'His speech on that occasion was composed by Leander (Labbe, Concilia, v, p. 997)'
claims.witness: O. M. Dalton's note to Gregory of Tours IX.15 (dalton1927 l.29212-29215)

claims.claim: Leovigild made 'duosque filios suos ex amissa conjuge, Ermenegildum et Recaredum, consortes regni'
claims.witness: John of Biclaro (PL72 l.64718-64722; mommsen1894 l.19937, per dossier)

claims.claim: John of Biclaro, a Goth, suffered under Leovigild for the Catholic faith and was exiled at Barcelona (Isidore, De viris illustribus, quoted by Mommsen; Mommsen: 'propter fidem catholicam iniurias regis Arianae addicti perpessus est et exilium Barcinonense'); his chronicle runs to Reccared's fourth year
'Hoc anno Leovegildus rex diem clausit extremum et filius eius Reccaredus cum tranquillitate regni eius sumit sceptra'
claims.witness: John of Biclaro (mommsen1894 l.20270-20271; OCR regularized)

claims.claim: Isidore: 'Aera DCXXIIII ... Levvigildo defuncto filius eius Recaredus regno est coronatus'; Mommsen brackets Reccared's reign 'a. 586-601' and writes 'Reccaredi (†a. 601)'; Krusch's margin to Fredegar IV.6 gives 586; Dalton: 'Leuvigild really died in the preceding year, 586'; Gardner: 'Leovigild died in 586'

'Reccaredus primo regni sui anno mense X catholicus deo iuvante efficitur et sacerdotes sectae Arrianae sapienti colloquio aggressus ratione potius quam imperio converti ad catholicam fidem facit gentemque omnium Gothorum et Suevorum ad unitatem et pacem revocat Christianae ecclesiae'
claims.witness: John of Biclaro (mommsen1894 l.20312-20316; OCR regularized); Mommsen's margin '587?' for the year-block (l.20273)

claims.claim: Gregory of Tours: Recared convoked the bishops of his own church and proposed they meet the Catholic bishops: 'discuss the doctrines of both parties, and let us discover which are true'; after the debate he 'submitted to the Catholic law, and received the sign of the blessed Cross with unction of holy chrism'
claims.witness: Gregory of Tours, History IX.15, tr. Dalton (dalton1927 l.18168-18209)

claims.claim: Fredegar: 'Richarid rex Gotorum divino amplectens amore, prius secrecius baptizatur'; he had the Arian books burned at Toledo and 'omnes Gothos ad christianam legem baptizare fecit'; Krusch's margin 587
claims.witness: Fredegar IV.8 (krusch1888 l.9380-9385; OCR regularized)

claims.claim: Gregory the Great: Leovigild commended Recharedus to Leander; after his father's death Rechared 'utterly renounced Arianism' and 'brought the whole nation of the Visegoths to the true faith'; 'he was the brother of a martyr, whose merits did help him'
claims.witness: Gregory the Great, Dialogues III.31 (gardner1911 l.8073-8098)

claims.claim: Barmby: Reccared 'had declared himself a Catholic a.d. 587'; Gardner: Rechared 'became a Catholic in the following year' after 586; Dalton: 'the conversion of Recared in 587'

Gregory to Reccared: 'I cannot express in words, most excellent son, how much I am delighted with thy work and thy life'; the whole nation of the Goths brought over 'from the error of Arian heresy to the firmness of a right faith', 'a new miracle in our days'; Ludwig M. Hartmann (editing after Paul Ewald's death) dates the letter (IX.228) August 599; Barmby 598-9
claims.witness: Register IX.122, tr. Barmby (npnf213 l.3870-3876); ewald-hartmann1893 l.15375-15384

claims.claim: Gregory, from the report of Probinus the presbyter: 'your Excellency having issued a certain ordinance against the perfidy of the Jews, those to whom it related attempted to bend the rectitude of your mind by offering a sum of money; which your Excellency scorned, and ... preferred innocence to gold'

Isidore: 'namque ille inreligiosus et bello promptissimus, hic fide pius et pace praeclarus'; 'Fuit autem placidus, mitis, egregiae bonitatis ... ut ... etiam malos ad affectum amoris sui adtraheret'; 'fidem enim rectae gloriae, quam initio regni percepit, novissime publica confessione paenitentiae cumulavit. Toleto fine pacifico transiit, qui regnauit annos XV'
claims.witness: Isidore, History of the Goths 52, 55-56 (mommsen1894 l.28264-28265, 28349-28368; OCR regularized)

claims.claim: Isidore: 'Aera DCXXXVIIII ... post Recaredum regem regnat Livva filius eius annis duobus, ignobili quidem matre progenitus'

Biclaro: at the council Reccared handed the bishops 'ordinem conversionis suae et omnium sacerdotum vel gentis Gothicae confessionem tomo scriptam manu sua', 'renovans temporibus nostris antiquum principem Constantinum Magnum' and Marcian
Biclaro: 'Reccaredus rex aliena a praecessoribus direpta et fisco sociata placabiliter restituit. ecclesiarum et monasteriorum conditor et ditator efficitur'
In his father's time Reccared, sent against the Franks in Gallia Narbonensis, drove them out and took the fort 'qui Hodierno vocatur' on the Rhone
claims.witness: John of Biclaro, Maurice III (mommsen1894 l.20251-20256)

claims.claim: Plots: 'Siuma episcopus et Segga' (Sunna and Seggo in Migne's text) were found out, Siuma exiled and Segga's hands cut off; 'Uldida episcopus cum Gosuintha regina insidiantes Reccaredo manifestantur', Uldila exiled, and Gosuintha 'catholicis semper infesta vitae tunc terminum dedit'
Gregory of Tours: 'Recared, his son, made covenant with Goiswinth, his father's widow, and recognized her as his mother'
claims.witness: Gregory of Tours IX.1, tr. Dalton (dalton1927 l.17554-17556)

claims.claim: Hermenegild's death: John, 'Hermenegildus in urbe Tarraconensi a Sisberto interficitur'; Gregory of Tours, 'Her lord Hermangild was slain by his father Leuvigild'; Gregory the Great, killed in prison by his father's officers after refusing an Arian bishop's communion; Dalton calls Gregory the Great's account 'fictitious'

Letter in Reccared's name to Gregory (Barmby IX.61; Hartmann IX.227a, from the Hispana collection): Barmby, 'The genuineness of this letter is considered doubtful. It may have been a forgery founded on Epistle CXXII', adding that its bad Latin is what Reccared's 'was not unlikely to be'; Ludwig M. Hartmann, editing after Paul Ewald's death, reports Gams calls it false and Mommsen agrees, thinking it made up from the next letter; he holds it carried 'sine dubio' by the priest Probinus, and thinks it 'male adservatam multisque locis corruptam', its rustic style fitting the time (the note's last word is cut off in the held lines)
claims.witness: npnf213 l.2254-2258; ewald-hartmann1893 l.15296-15300, 15333-15337 (OCR regularized)

contested_claims.claim: How and when Reccared became Catholic
contested_claims.sides: Reccared, at the council: not many days after his father's death (acts l.36620-36623). John of Biclaro: tenth month of his first year, by wise talk with the Arian clergy (mommsen1894 l.20312-20316). Gregory of Tours: after a debate of the two sides' bishops, receiving chrism (dalton1927 l.18168-18209). Fredegar: first a secret baptism (krusch1888 l.9380-9381). Gregory the Great: through Leander's counsel and his martyred brother's merits (gardner1911 l.8073-8098). Barmby, Gardner and Dalton give 587.

contested_claims.claim: Whose words the book of faith is
contested_claims.sides: The acts: offered by the king, written in his voice, read by a notary (acts l.36628-36632); John of Biclaro: the confession 'tomo scriptam manu sua episcopis porrigens', which can be read as written by his own hand or handed over by his own hand (mommsen1894 l.20394-20396). Dalton: the speech was composed by Leander, citing Labbe (dalton1927 l.29212-29215).

contested_claims.claim: Whether Leovigild entrusted Reccared to Leander
contested_claims.sides: Gregory the Great says so (gardner1911 l.8073-8080). R. Altamira, reported by Dalton: no evidence in contemporary documents (dalton1927 l.29043-29047).

contested_claims.claim: How Hermenegild died
contested_claims.sides: John of Biclaro: killed by Sisbert at Tarragona (mommsen1894 l.20246). Gregory of Tours: slain by his father (dalton1927 l.16509-16510). Gregory the Great: put to death in prison on his father's order for refusing Arian communion (gardner1911 l.8036-8057), an account Dalton calls fictitious (l.28849-28851).

contested_claims.claim: The letter in Reccared's name to Gregory
contested_claims.sides: Doubted: Barmby, 'considered doubtful', perhaps a forgery founded on Ep. CXXII, though 'The Latin in the original is in many parts incorrect and ungrammatical; being such indeed Reccared's was not unlikely to be' (npnf213 l.2254-2258). Gams: false, its rustic style unfit for a letter to the pope; Mommsen agrees, thinking it made up from the next letter (both reported by Ludwig M. Hartmann, editing after Paul Ewald's death, l.15334-15336). Genuine: Hartmann heads it 'translata sine dubio per Probinum presbyterum' (l.15333) and answers 'equidem credo et hanc ep. male adservatam multisque locis corruptam esse et rusticitatem stili huic tempori ...' (l.15337; the note's last words fall outside the held lines).

contested_claims.claim: The year of his death
contested_claims.sides: Isidore: fifteen years' reign, Liuva succeeding in era 639 (mommsen1894 l.28367-28372); Mommsen: 601 (l.21946); Brehaut: 'd. 601' (per dossier, brehaut1912 l.711). Perez in PL83: Reccared died 600 and Liuva succeeded era 639 = 601 (PL83 l.122864-122870), contradicting himself.

absent_details.note: No usable held source gives them. The only birth place, 'Reccaredus Hispali nascitur', is in the PL80 chronicle under the name of Maximus of Saragossa, which the Bollandists class among deceptive later inventions ('nullius fidei ista apud nos sunt', Acta Sanctorum Junii V l.6385-6387); not used.

absent_details.detail: A complete English translation of the Toledo III acts
absent_details.note: None held; the 1808 file header says no public-domain English exists. Percival (NPNF 14) translates only canon II and the anathema on the Universal Church (npnf214 l.13703-13741). The brief's telling of the tomus and subscription is a paraphrase of the Latin.

absent_details.detail: An Arian-side account of his reign
absent_details.note: None used here. The witnesses (the acts, John of Biclaro, Isidore, Gregory of Tours, Gregory the Great, Fredegar) are Catholic.

absent_details.detail: Who baptized, anointed or crowned him
absent_details.note: No usable held source names the minister. Gregory of Tours mentions chrism without a name (dalton1927 l.18207-18209). The crowning by Euphemius and Leander and anointing by Masona is only in the PL80 'Maximus' chronicle; not used. The PL96 epigrams are marked supposititious by their editor; not used.

absent_details.detail: The mother of his son Liuva
absent_details.note: Isidore calls her of humble birth and does not name her (mommsen1894 l.28372). No held line identifies her with Queen Baddo.

claims.claim: The students left the school 'distribuant les objets qu'ils avaient; ils emportaient des evangiles et des croix sur des voiles noirs, avec des encensoirs; et ils sortirent de la ville en prieres, et en chantant les hymnes des rogations; ils etaient environ trois cents'; they were moved by Sabrisho's accepting Hnana's word over the metropolitan's; 'Il ne resta dans l'Ecole que vingt personnes et a peine autant d'enfants'
claims.witness: Chronicle of Seert LXXIV, tr. Scher (chronicle-of-seert po13 scher1919 l.28671-28710; OCR 'TEcoIe', 'eiiviron'); a hostile account

claims.claim: 'Le docteur de Nisibe etait alors Hnana d'Adiabene, disciple de Moise; depuis longtemps, il etait a l'Ecole, curieux de la lecture des ecrits heterodoxes; il avait explique des choses contrairement a Theodore l'interprete; il s'etait ecarte de la verite pour adherer a des doctrines heretiques'
claims.witness: Chronicle of Seert LXXIV (chronicle-of-seert po13 scher1919 l.28601-28606; OCR 'TEcole', 'rinterprete'); hostile

claims.claim: Abdisho of Nisibis says of Henana that he 'alios plures libros edidit, qui propter Commentatorem repudiati sunt', which Assemani glosses as his departing from Theodore's sense in expounding Scripture
claims.witness: Assemani, Bibliotheca orientalis III.1 (l.15165-15171; OCR 'Sturarum', 'recellit'); Badger's English of the same entry, 'many other works condemned by Theodorus of Mopsuestia' (badger v2 l.17705-17706)

claims.claim: He left Theodore of Mopsuestia's reading of Scripture: carried by two held witnesses, both hostile or of the opposing tradition within his church (the Chronicle of Seert; Abdisho)
claims.witness: Seert l.28603-28604; Assemani l.15165-15171. Scher: 'les Nestoriens ont toujours accusé Hnana d'avoir abandonné dans ses commentaires les sentences de Théodore' (barhadbeshabba cause po4 scher1908 l.21073-21075)

claims.claim: Scher: 'Hnana devint maitre de l'Ecole de Nisibe en 572'; 'Hnana succéda en 572 à Abraham'
claims.witness: Scher's notes (chronicle-of-seert po13 scher1919 l.28620-28621; barhadbeshabba cause po4 scher1908 l.21023)

claims.claim: Chabot: Henana d'Adiabène, 'le célèbre docteur de l'Ecole de Nisibe' who taught there under the patriarchate of Ezekiel 'vers 570'
claims.witness: Chabot's note to canon II of Ishoyahb I (synodicon-orientale chabot1902 l.26750-26757, two columns interleaved)

claims.claim: When Gregory became metropolitan of Nisibis he reproached Hnana, 'alors Gregoire condamna les livres qu'il avait composes'; Gregory wrote to the catholicos Sabrisho; Hnana wrote to Sabrisho 'une lettre, dans laquelle il se jouait de lui'; the Fathers excommunicated Hnana, but 'le catholicos ... accueillit favorablement la lettre de Hnana'; Gregory, 'apres avoir secoue la poussiere de ses sandales a la porte de Nisibe, il quitta la ville'
claims.witness: Chronicle of Seert LXXIV (chronicle-of-seert po13 scher1919 l.28607-28666); hostile

claims.claim: Gregory is Gregory of Kashkar ('B. Gregor (v. Kaskar)'), a native of Kashkar, ordained metropolitan of Nisibis by Sabrisho
claims.witness: Braun, Buch der Synhados (synodicon-orientale braun1900 l.13699, 13713-13716)

claims.claim: In Babai's Life of George a monk says Henana is 'cet homme qui enseigne le fatalisme, prèche la fatalité', 'Il fait Dieu limité, passible, mortel, divisé en parties', 'nie la résurrection des corps et [n'admet] le salut que pour les âmes'; Babai reports what 'leur maître Henana' said: 'Le sort et la fatalité sont cause de tout et tout est conduit par les étoiles', and calls him 'Henana l'hérétique, le chaldéen et l'origéniste'; Babai sets out the 'doctrines impies qu'il partage avec les Sévériens, en professant qu'il y a dans le Christ une nature et une hypostase, et en introduisant la passibilité dans la divinité'
claims.witness: Babai the Great, Life of George, extracts tr. Chabot (synodicon-orientale chabot1902 l.42093-42118, 42142-42144); one hostile witness. Labourt counts three charges: 'il était chaldéen, origéniste et hérétique (au point de vue de l'Incarnation)' (labourt1904 l.15734-15736)

claims.claim: The Life of George is 'composée par saint Rabban Mar Babai, supérieur du couvent qui est sur le mont Izala'
claims.witness: Chabot (synodicon-orientale chabot1902 l.42082-42083)

claims.claim: George, born Mihramgouënasp, took the name George at baptism and made his profession in the convent of Dadisho on Mount Izla; Labourt names 'Georges le martyr' among the disciples of the Izla superiors
claims.witness: Chabot (synodicon-orientale chabot1902 l.42084-42088); Labourt (labourt1904 l.12224-12227)

claims.claim: Braun: the only contemporary account is 'der leidenschaftliche Babai von Jzala'; 'Wenn wir dessen Uebertreibungen und Widersprüche zu berichtigen suchen, so scheinen die anstössigsten Punkte die Lehren über Astrologie (nach B. Chaldäertum) u. Apokatastasis'
claims.witness: Braun (synodicon-orientale braun1900 l.13690-13696)

claims.claim: Labourt calls Babai 'son antagoniste Babaï le Grand'; 'Est-ce calomnieusement que Babaï attribue à Henana l'opinion suivante ... ? Nous ne saurions le dire. Cette imputation n'est cependant pas invraisemblable'
claims.witness: Labourt, Le christianisme dans l'empire perse (labourt1904 l.15713-15714, 15747-15751)

claims.claim: The synod acts never name Henana: 'Die Synodalacten erwähnen jedoch den H. ... nirgends'; Braun reads canon 2 of Ishoyahb's synod (585/6) as 'bereits deutlich gegen Hannana gerichtet, ohne ihn noch [zu nennen]'; the defence of Theodore 'gilt vor Allem den Theopaschiten'

Chabot reads canon II of Ishoyahb's synod as 'très probablement' aimed at a commentary by Henana; Labourt reads the canon of 585 as aimed at those who 'à la suite du docteur Henana de Nisibe' refused Theodore's exegesis, and the anathema of Sabrisho as directed 'contre lui'
claims.witness: Chabot (synodicon-orientale chabot1902 l.26750-26757); Labourt (l.11616-11620, 15736-15745)

claims.claim: Timothy I says the catholicos Sabrisho condemned 'Hanani Adiabeni scripta'
claims.witness: Abdisho, Collection of canons IX.6, quoting Timothy I, ed. Mai (mai1838 l.18708-18716, 18864-18866); Assemani l.14926-14931

claims.claim: Labourt: 'Sabriso' se prononça cependant contre eux [the Henanians] dans le synode général qu'il tint au mois d'Yar ... (mai 596)'; Chabot: Henana's works 'furent condamnés à différentes reprises' by the patriarchs
claims.witness: Labourt (labourt1904 l.12231-12234); Chabot (synodicon-orientale chabot1902 l.26755-26761)

claims.claim: Mari: 'Floruerunt Nisibi inter doctores Jesujabus et Abrahamus Haddadi filius, et Hannanus qui auditores numerabat octingentos'
claims.witness: Mari ibn Sulayman, tr. Gismondi (gismondi1899 l.13822-13824; OCR 'numorabat oclingenlos')

claims.claim: Barhadbeshabba: 'Il fut remplacé par Hnana d'Adiabène, homme orné d'humilité, et de tous les dons d'instruction qu'exige l'œuvre de l'interprétation'; 'il s'appliquait jour et nuit à la lecture et à l'interprétation des Écritures'; 'Nous prions tous Dieu de prolonger ses jours'; 'Il est doux, miséricordieux, patient et ne cherche pas sa propre gloire comme les autres'
claims.witness: Barhadbeshabba, Cause of the Foundation of the Schools, tr. Scher (barhadbeshabba cause po4 scher1908 l.21006-21007, 21043-21044, 21121, 21133-21134); a friendly witness; the later lines speak of 'lui' in the continuing passage on Hnana

claims.claim: Barhadbeshabba wrote 'du vivant même de son maître Hnana'; he was among the students who left; he later became bishop of Halwan
claims.witness: Scher's introduction (barhadbeshabba cause po4 scher1908 l.16970-16975, 16994-17003)

claims.claim: Scher: 'Il est probable que l'auteur dissimule ici la vérité pour louer son maître auprès de ses coreligionnaires'; Gregory 'était ennemi acharné de Hnana'
claims.witness: Scher's note (barhadbeshabba cause po4 scher1908 l.21073-21079)

claims.claim: New canons were added in 590, 'quando Simeone era metropolita di Nisibi, e maestro della scuola era Hannànà'
claims.witness: Guidi (statuti-della-scuola-di-nisibi guidi1890 l.9918-9921)

claims.claim: Aha, Isaiah of Tahal and Meskena 'Arbaya, 'disciples de Hnana', refused to go with Gregory's friends
claims.witness: Chronicle of Seert LXXIV (chronicle-of-seert po13 scher1919 l.28714-28716)

claims.claim: Abdisho lists commentaries on the Psalms, Genesis, Job, Proverbs, Ecclesiastes, the Song of Solomon, the Twelve Prophets, Mark and Paul, an exposition of the faith and sacraments, and treatises on feasts
claims.witness: Badger's English of Abdisho's catalogue (badger v2 l.17698-17706); Scher's note (barhadbeshabba cause po4 scher1908 l.21080-21086)

claims.claim: Scher: 'Il ne nous est parvenu de ces ouvrages que les traités sur les Rogations et le vendredi d'or'
claims.witness: Scher's note (barhadbeshabba cause po4 scher1908 l.21084-21086); the treatises are edited in Patrologia Orientalis 7, which is not held (advertised in po09 l.41505-41508)

claims.claim: His death: Scher says he died under Sabrisho (596-604) and elsewhere that he was alive in 610; Babai writes of 'la seconde mort' of Henana, which Chabot reads as already dead
claims.witness: Scher (barhadbeshabba cause po4 scher1908 l.21023-21024, 21734); Babai tr. Chabot (synodicon-orientale chabot1902 l.42221-42222, Chabot's note l.42237-42240)

contested_claims.claim: What Henana taught
contested_claims.sides: Babai the Great alone, in the Life of George of Izla: fatalism, astrology ('Chaldean'), Origenism, denial of bodily resurrection, and one nature and one hypostasis in Christ with the Severians (chabot1902 l.42093-42118, 42142-42144, 42218-42222). Braun calls Babai passionate and corrects for his exaggerations and contradictions (braun1900 l.13690-13696); Labourt calls Babai his antagonist and cannot say whether the charge is slander, though not implausible (labourt1904 l.15713, 15747-15751). His pupil Barhadbeshabba says nothing of heresy and praises his interpretation (scher1908 l.21006-21050); Scher thinks the pupil probably hid the truth (l.21073).

contested_claims.claim: When Henana died
contested_claims.sides: Scher: under Sabrisho, 596-604 (scher1908 l.21023-21024); Scher: still alive in 610, from the Chronicle of Seert (l.21734); Scher on Seert: alive in 612 by that author, though Babai seems to say he was already dead (seert l.29901-29904); Babai as read by Chabot: already dead (chabot1902 l.42221-42222, 42237-42240).

contested_claims.claim: Whether Sabrisho supported or condemned Henana
contested_claims.sides: Chronicle of Seert: Sabrisho 'accueillit favorablement la lettre de Hnana' and would not confirm the Fathers' sentence (seert scher1919 l.28655-28660). Timothy I, quoted by Abdisho: Sabrisho condemned 'Hanani Adiabeni scripta' (mai1838 l.18862-18866). Labourt: Sabrisho's synod of May 596 pronounced against the Henanians (labourt1904 l.12231-12234). Chabot: his works were condemned more than once by the patriarchs (chabot1902 l.26755-26761).

absent_details.note: Scher says his treatises on the Rogations and Golden Friday survive (barhadbeshabba cause po4 scher1908 l.21084-21086); they are edited in Patrologia Orientalis 7, which is not held (advertised in po09 l.41505-41508). Guidi's Syriac statutes are not recovered by OCR and he quotes no canon of Henana's in Italian.
No held ancient line gives either. 572 is Scher's reckoning; Chabot's is about 570; see the death contested_claim.

The synods dated 585, 596 and 605 (Chabot l.26590-26712, 30464-31377, 31388-31700) do not name Henana; Braun says so (braun1900 l.13708-13728). Their reference to him is Chabot's, Braun's and Labourt's reading.

absent_details.detail: A second witness to Babai's doctrinal charges
absent_details.note: None held. Babai's De Unione and Evagrius commentary are cited by Braun and Labourt but not held; the Chronicle of Seert speaks of 'doctrines heretiques' without naming them.

claims.claim: The king sat in the open air on Thanet 'lest, according to an ancient superstition, if they practised any magical arts, they might impose upon him'; they came 'bearing a silver cross for their banner, and the image of our Lord and Saviour painted on a board; and singing the litany'
claims.witness: Bede, HE I.25 (bede giles1903 l.1922-1965)

claims.claim: Ethelbert: 'Your words and promises are very fair, but as they are new to us, and of uncertain import, I cannot approve of them so far as to forsake that which I have so long followed with the whole English nation'; he let them stay and preach
claims.witness: Bede, HE I.25 (bede giles1903 l.1969-1985); the king's speech in Bede's telling

claims.claim: Gregory calls him 'quondam monasterii mei praepositum, nunc fratrem et coepiscopum nostrum' and 'monasterii mei monachum'
claims.witness: Gregory to Syagrius, Register IX.222 (gregory-great registrum t2 pars1 ewald-hartmann1893 l.14758-14762); Gregory to Eulogius (gregory-great epistolae-selectae turchi1907 l.9306-9311)

claims.claim: 'In the year 596, Pope Gregory sent Augustine with monks into Britain'; 'In the year 597, the aforesaid teachers arrived in Britain'
claims.witness: Bede's chronicle summary (bede giles1903 l.15271-15277)

claims.claim: On the journey they were 'seized with a sudden fear' of 'a barbarous, fierce, and unbelieving nation, to whose very language they were strangers', and sent Augustine back to Gregory
claims.witness: Bede, HE I.23 (bede giles1903 l.1813-1830)

claims.claim: Gregory's letter: 'When Augustine, your chief, returns, whom we also constitute your abbat, humbly obey him in all things'
claims.witness: Gregory, as Bede copies the letter (bede giles1903 l.1843-1848); Latin 'Augustino praeposito vestro, quem et abbatem vobis constituimus' (gregory-great epistolae-selectae turchi1907 l.9116-9119)

claims.claim: The king 'believed and was baptized'; 'he compelled none to embrace Christianity'; he gave his teachers a residence in Canterbury
claims.witness: Bede, HE I.26 (bede giles1903 l.2033-2056)

claims.claim: 'In solemnitate autem Dominicae nativitatis ... plusquam decem milia Angli ab eodem nuntiati sunt fratre et coepiscopo nostro baptizati'
claims.witness: Gregory to Eulogius of Alexandria (gregory-great epistolae-selectae turchi1907 l.9328-9333)

claims.claim: Gregory: 'Qui data a me licentia a Germaniarum episcopis episcopus factus cum eorum quoque solaciis ad praedictam gentem in finem mundi perductus est', before the Christmas baptisms by 'fratre et coepiscopo nostro'
claims.witness: Gregory to Eulogius of Alexandria (gregory-great epistolae-selectae turchi1907 l.9309-9326, 9331-9332)

claims.claim: Augustine 'repaired to Arles, and ... was ordained archbishop of the English nation, by Aetherius, archbishop of that city'
claims.witness: Bede, HE I.27 (bede giles1903 l.2063-2066)

claims.claim: 'Aetherius was really archbishop of Lyons'
claims.witness: L. Cecil Jane's note (bede giles1903 l.15827)

claims.claim: Augustine, after baptizing Ethelbert with his people on Christmas 597, went to Gaul 'ut a Vergilio Arelatensi episcopus consecraretur'
claims.witness: Nicola Turchi's note 26 (gregory-great epistolae-selectae turchi1907 l.9318-9324)

claims.claim: Second question: 'Whereas the faith is one and the same, why are there different customs in different churches? and why is one custom of masses observed in the holy Roman church, and another in the Galilean church?'
claims.witness: Augustine's question as Bede copies it (bede giles1903 l.2127-2132; 'Galilean' is the edition's word for Gallican)

claims.claim: Gregory: 'For things are not to be loved for the sake of places, but places for the sake of good things'
claims.witness: Gregory's answer, in Bede (bede giles1903 l.2136-2150)

claims.claim: 'De hac epistula, an genuina sit, saepe disputatur'; '... non dubito, quin genuina sit'; Mommsen holds 'non integram epistulam, sed excerpta tantum nobis asservata esse'
claims.witness: Ludwig Hartmann's note to Register XI.56a, in the volume he edited after Paul Ewald's death (title page gregory-great registrum t2 pars2 ewald-hartmann1895 l.103-106); the note is in his first person ('non dubito') and names Ewald in the third ('Ewald coniecit', l.12696-12697) (l.12643, 12700-12706; OCR rough)

claims.claim: Bede's copy 'may be regarded as the most authentic'; Boniface asked Nothelm for a copy since none could be found at Rome
claims.witness: James Barmby's note (npnf213 l.7292-7310)

claims.claim: Boniface writes to Nothelm that the letter 'in scrinio Romanae aecclesiae ... quaesita non inveniebatur'; Hartmann dates the letter 'a. 735' in his preface and 'ante a. 741' in his note to XI.56a
claims.witness: Ludwig Hartmann's preface, quoting Boniface, in the volume he edited after Paul Ewald's death (title page gregory-great registrum t2 pars2 ewald-hartmann1895 l.103-106; preface l.195-203, signed by Hartmann l.178-181); his note to XI.56a (l.12690); Boniface's letter is not itself held

claims.claim: Gregory sent Augustine the pall and directed him to 'ordain twelve bishops, who shall be subject to your jurisdiction', and a bishop for York who 'shall also ordain twelve bishops'
claims.witness: Gregory's letter, in Bede, HE I.29 (bede giles1903 l.2776-2828)

claims.claim: Gregory's letter on his miracles: 'it is necessary that you rejoice with fear, and tremble whilst you rejoice'
claims.witness: Gregory's letter, in Bede, HE I.31 (bede giles1903 l.2944-2958)

claims.claim: Gregory: 'as for all the bishops of Britain, we commit them to your care'
claims.witness: Gregory's answer to the seventh question, in Bede (bede giles1903 l.2334-2338)

claims.claim: With Ethelbert's help Augustine drew the British bishops to a conference 'at a place which is to this day called Augustine's Ac, that is, Augustine's Oak'; after a blind man was healed, the Britons 'desired that a second synod might be appointed'
claims.witness: Bede, HE II.2 (bede giles1903 l.3563-3617)

claims.claim: Before the second synod they consulted a hermit: 'if at your approach he shall rise up to you, hear him submissively'; 'when they came, Augustine was sitting on a chair'; they refused him; Bede does not name the place of this synod
claims.witness: Bede, HE II.2 (bede giles1903 l.3619-3672)

claims.claim: Augustine 'is said, in a threatening manner, to have foretold' that if they would not preach to the English 'they should at their hands undergo the vengeance of death'
claims.witness: Bede, HE II.2 (bede giles1903 l.3672-3682), with Bede's own hedge

claims.claim: Bede calls the Britons 'that perfidious nation'
claims.witness: Bede, HE II.2 (bede giles1903 l.3683-3685); a hostile witness on the Britons

claims.claim: In 604 Augustine ordained Mellitus and Justus; 'After this, the beloved of God, Father Augustine, died'
claims.witness: Bede, HE II.3 (bede giles1903 l.3734-3765)

claims.claim: Epitaph: 'Here rests the Lord Augustine, first archbishop of Canterbury ... died the 26th day of May, in the reign of the same king'
claims.witness: Bede, HE II.3 (bede giles1903 l.3784-3791)

claims.claim: 'Laurentius a. 606 Augustino episcopus successit'
claims.witness: Ludwig Hartmann's note, in the volume he edited after Paul Ewald's death (title page gregory-great registrum t2 pars2 ewald-hartmann1895 l.103-106; note l.10690-10693)

claims.claim: Jane: 'Augustine was a Benedictine and trained under Gregory at the monastery of St. Anthony, Rome'
claims.witness: L. Cecil Jane's note (bede giles1903 l.15824-15825); no held letter of Gregory names the monastery

contested_claims.claim: Who ordained him in Gaul
sides: Bede: Aetherius, archbishop of Arles (bede giles1903 l.2063-2066); Jane's note says Aetherius was really of Lyons (l.15827)
Nicola Turchi: Vergilius of Arles (turchi1907 l.9322-9324)
Gregory: only 'a Germaniarum episcopis' (turchi1907 l.9309-9311)

contested_claims.claim: Whether the answers to Augustine's questions are genuine and whole
sides: Ludwig Hartmann, editing after Paul Ewald's death: often disputed, but genuine (ewald-hartmann1895 title page l.103-106; note l.12643, 12703-12705)
Mommsen, reported by Hartmann: only extracts survive (l.12705-12706)
Barmby: Bede's copy the most authentic; later copies add an interpolated question (npnf213 l.7292-7310, 7554-7557)

contested_claims.claim: Whether he was made bishop before or after reaching the English
sides: Gregory to Eulogius: made bishop by the bishops of the Germanies and then brought to the English (turchi1907 l.9309-9326)
Bede: went to Arles after the king's baptism (bede giles1903 l.2033-2066)
Nicola Turchi's note follows Bede's order: after the Christmas baptism of 597 (turchi1907 l.9318-9324)

absent_details.note: No held ancient source gives it. The epitaph gives 26 May; Bede tells the death after the ordinations he dates to 604. Searched Bede (Giles and Plummer), the two Register volumes, Turchi and Barmby.

absent_details.detail: Letters or writings of his own
absent_details.note: None held beyond his questions, which survive inside Gregory's answers as Bede and the Register give them.
